body: One Nation would abolish Australia's permanent parent visas and cut the yearly refugee intake from 20,000 places to 2,000 if it were in government, party leader Pauline Hanson announced in Canberra on Wednesday.

Parent visas are one of the main ways migrant families, including many Indian-Australian families, bring mothers and fathers to live with them permanently. One Nation is a minor party, and the plan would need to pass federal parliament before anything changed.

ul: Scrap the permanent parent visa program. This financial year's cap is 8,500 parent and aged parent visas, up from 7,060 last year, the ABC reported.
Refund the application fees of people already in the queue. The ABC put the queue at about 157,000 people; AAP reported about 150,000.

Parents already in Australia would have to leave unless they applied for a different way to stay, the ABC reported. AAP reported they would need a separate visa paid for by their family rather than the taxpayer.
Cut the refugee and humanitarian intake from 20,000 places a year to 2,000.
These changes add to the plan One Nation announced in September: cutting 750,000 temporary visa holders over three years, then capping net overseas migration at 130,000 a year.

body: "It's called tough love, but my love is for the Australian people first and foremost," Senator Hanson said, according to the ABC. She said Australia could not provide enough aged care beds for its own people, and that families who wanted their parents here should pay the cost themselves.

She said scrapping parent visas and most of the refugee intake would cut migration spending by $100 billion over a decade. The ABC reported that figure is based on One Nation's own analysis of Treasury data and has not been costed by the Parliamentary Budget Office.
Senator Hanson denied the refugee cut targeted Muslim-majority countries, AAP reported. Refugees from Syria, Afghanistan and Iraq make up most of the places in the current program.
The average wait for a parent or aged parent visa is 42 years, and 18 years for a contributory parent visa, where the family pays far more upfront, the ABC reported.

ul: Labor: Foreign Minister Penny Wong called ending parent visas "very harsh" and said Australia had a duty to accept refugees, the ABC reported. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the government remained committed to its target of bringing net overseas migration down to 225,000, and AAP reported he warned One Nation's plans risked Australia losing skilled workers.

Coalition: Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson said One Nation could not be trusted on immigration because it announces a number and then changes it, AAP reported. The Coalition has promised to halve the refugee intake to 10,000 and more than halve net overseas migration, according to the ABC.

body: One Nation is also contesting Victoria's state election on 28 November, but visa rules are set by the federal government, not the states.

body.note: Nothing changes for parent visa applicants because of this announcement. Parent visa rules stay as they are unless federal parliament changes them. This is a news report, not migration advice: check the Department of Home Affairs website or speak to a registered migration agent about your own situation.

en.dek: Pauline Hanson says people already in the queue would get their fees back, and parents already here would have to leave unless they find another way to stay. Penny Wong called the plan 'very harsh'.

body: वन नेशन पार्टी की नेता पॉलीन हैन्सन ने बुधवार को कैनबरा में घोषणा की कि सरकार में आने पर उनकी पार्टी ऑस्ट्रेलिया के स्थायी पैरेंट वीज़ा खत्म कर देगी और हर साल आने वाले शरणार्थियों की संख्या 20,000 से घटाकर 2,000 कर देगी।

पैरेंट वीज़ा प्रवासी परिवारों के लिए, जिनमें कई भारतीय-ऑस्ट्रेलियाई परिवार भी हैं, अपने माता-पिता को स्थायी रूप से साथ रखने के मुख्य रास्तों में से एक है। वन नेशन एक छोटी पार्टी है, और कुछ भी बदलने से पहले इस योजना को संघीय संसद से पास होना होगा।

body.h: वन नेशन क्या प्रस्ताव रख रही है

ul: स्थायी पैरेंट वीज़ा कार्यक्रम खत्म करना। ABC के अनुसार इस वित्तीय वर्ष की सीमा 8,500 पैरेंट और एज्ड पैरेंट वीज़ा है, जो पिछले साल 7,060 थी।
कतार में पहले से मौजूद लोगों की आवेदन फ़ीस लौटाना। ABC के अनुसार कतार में लगभग 1,57,000 लोग हैं; AAP ने यह संख्या लगभग 1,50,000 बताई।

ABC के अनुसार, जो माता-पिता पहले से ऑस्ट्रेलिया में हैं उन्हें जाना होगा, जब तक वे रहने के किसी दूसरे रास्ते के लिए आवेदन न करें। AAP के अनुसार उन्हें एक अलग वीज़ा की ज़रूरत होगी जिसका खर्च करदाता नहीं, बल्कि परिवार उठाएगा।
शरणार्थी और मानवीय कार्यक्रम को हर साल 20,000 स्थानों से घटाकर 2,000 करना।
ये बदलाव वन नेशन की सितंबर में घोषित योजना के अलावा हैं: तीन साल में 7,50,000 अस्थायी वीज़ा धारकों को कम करना, और फिर शुद्ध विदेशी प्रवासन को हर साल 1,30,000 तक सीमित करना।

body: ABC के अनुसार सीनेटर हैन्सन ने कहा, "इसे सख़्त प्यार कहते हैं, लेकिन मेरा प्यार सबसे पहले ऑस्ट्रेलियाई लोगों के लिए है।" उन्होंने कहा कि ऑस्ट्रेलिया अपने ही लोगों के लिए पर्याप्त एज्ड केयर बेड नहीं दे पा रहा, और जो परिवार अपने माता-पिता को यहाँ लाना चाहते हैं उन्हें खर्च ख़ुद उठाना चाहिए।

उन्होंने कहा कि पैरेंट वीज़ा और ज़्यादातर शरणार्थी कार्यक्रम खत्म करने से दस साल में प्रवासन पर खर्च 100 अरब डॉलर कम होगा। ABC के अनुसार यह आँकड़ा ट्रेज़री के आँकड़ों के वन नेशन के अपने विश्लेषण पर आधारित है, और पार्लियामेंटरी बजट ऑफ़िस ने इसकी लागत का आकलन नहीं किया है।

AAP के अनुसार सीनेटर हैन्सन ने इस बात से इनकार किया कि शरणार्थियों में कटौती मुस्लिम-बहुल देशों को निशाना बनाती है। मौजूदा कार्यक्रम में ज़्यादातर स्थान सीरिया, अफ़ग़ानिस्तान और इराक़ के शरणार्थियों के हैं।

body.h: परिवार अभी कितना इंतज़ार करते हैं

body: ABC के अनुसार पैरेंट या एज्ड पैरेंट वीज़ा का औसत इंतज़ार 42 साल है, और कॉन्ट्रिब्यूटरी पैरेंट वीज़ा का 18 साल, जिसमें परिवार पहले ही काफ़ी ज़्यादा भुगतान करता है।

ul: लेबर: ABC के अनुसार विदेश मंत्री पेनी वोंग ने पैरेंट वीज़ा खत्म करने को "बहुत कठोर" बताया और कहा कि शरणार्थियों को स्वीकार करना ऑस्ट्रेलिया का कर्तव्य है। गृह मामलों के मंत्री टोनी बर्क ने कहा कि सरकार शुद्ध विदेशी प्रवासन को 2,25,000 तक लाने के अपने लक्ष्य पर क़ायम है, और AAP के अनुसार उन्होंने चेतावनी दी कि वन नेशन की योजनाओं से ऑस्ट्रेलिया कुशल कामगार खो सकता है।

गठबंधन: AAP के अनुसार शैडो ट्रेज़रर टिम विल्सन ने कहा कि प्रवासन पर वन नेशन पर भरोसा नहीं किया जा सकता, क्योंकि वह एक संख्या की घोषणा करके फिर उसे बदल देती है। ABC के अनुसार गठबंधन ने शरणार्थियों की संख्या आधी करके 10,000 करने और शुद्ध विदेशी प्रवासन को आधे से ज़्यादा घटाने का वादा किया है।

body: वन नेशन 28 नवंबर के विक्टोरिया राज्य चुनाव में भी हिस्सा ले रही है, लेकिन वीज़ा के नियम राज्य नहीं, संघीय सरकार तय करती है।

body.note: इस घोषणा से पैरेंट वीज़ा आवेदकों के लिए कुछ नहीं बदलता। जब तक संघीय संसद नियम न बदले, पैरेंट वीज़ा के नियम वैसे ही रहेंगे। यह एक समाचार रिपोर्ट है, प्रवासन सलाह नहीं: अपनी स्थिति के बारे में गृह मामलों के विभाग की वेबसाइट देखें या किसी पंजीकृत माइग्रेशन एजेंट से बात करें।

hi.dek: पॉलीन हैन्सन का कहना है कि कतार में मौजूद लोगों को उनकी फ़ीस लौटा दी जाएगी, और जो माता-पिता पहले से यहाँ हैं उन्हें जाना होगा, जब तक उन्हें रहने का कोई दूसरा रास्ता न मिले। पेनी वोंग ने इस योजना को 'बहुत कठोर' बताया।
hi.headline: हैन्सन ने कहा, वन नेशन पैरेंट वीज़ा खत्म करेगी और शरणार्थियों की संख्या 90 प्रतिशत घटाएगी

caption.hi: वन नेशन की नेता पॉलीन हैन्सन, दिसंबर 2016 में ली गई तस्वीर।
caption.pa: ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਦੀ ਆਗੂ ਪੌਲੀਨ ਹੈਨਸਨ, ਦਸੰਬਰ 2016 ਵਿੱਚ ਲਈ ਗਈ ਤਸਵੀਰ।

body: ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਪਾਰਟੀ ਦੀ ਆਗੂ ਪੌਲੀਨ ਹੈਨਸਨ ਨੇ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਕੈਨਬਰਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਐਲਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਕਿ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਣ 'ਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਾਰਟੀ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਦੇ ਸਥਾਈ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਕਰ ਦੇਵੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਸਾਲ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਸ਼ਰਨਾਰਥੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ 20,000 ਤੋਂ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ 2,000 ਕਰ ਦੇਵੇਗੀ।

ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਸੀ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਈ ਭਾਰਤੀ-ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆਈ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਵੀ ਹਨ, ਆਪਣੇ ਮਾਪਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪੱਕੇ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖਣ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਰਾਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਹੈ। ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਇੱਕ ਛੋਟੀ ਪਾਰਟੀ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਕੁਝ ਵੀ ਬਦਲਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਇਸ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਘੀ ਸੰਸਦ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪਾਸ ਹੋਣਾ ਪਵੇਗਾ।

body.h: ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਕੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਤਾਵ ਰੱਖ ਰਹੀ ਹੈ

ul: ਸਥਾਈ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਕਰਨਾ। ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਤੀ ਸਾਲ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ 8,500 ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਅਤੇ ਏਜਡ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਸਾਲ 7,060 ਸੀ।
ਕਤਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਫ਼ੀਸ ਵਾਪਸ ਕਰਨਾ। ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਕਤਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਗਭਗ 1,57,000 ਲੋਕ ਹਨ; AAP ਨੇ ਇਹ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਲਗਭਗ 1,50,000 ਦੱਸੀ।

ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, ਜੋ ਮਾਪੇ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਨ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਣਾ ਪਵੇਗਾ, ਜਦੋਂ ਤੱਕ ਉਹ ਰਹਿਣ ਦੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਰਾਹ ਲਈ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਨਾ ਦੇਣ। AAP ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਪਵੇਗੀ ਜਿਸ ਦਾ ਖ਼ਰਚ ਟੈਕਸਦਾਤਾ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸਗੋਂ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਚੁੱਕੇਗਾ।
ਸ਼ਰਨਾਰਥੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਹਰ ਸਾਲ 20,000 ਥਾਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ 2,000 ਕਰਨਾ।
ਇਹ ਬਦਲਾਅ ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਦੀ ਸਤੰਬਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਐਲਾਨੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਹਨ: ਤਿੰਨ ਸਾਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ 7,50,000 ਆਰਜ਼ੀ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਧਾਰਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਘਟਾਉਣਾ, ਅਤੇ ਫਿਰ ਸ਼ੁੱਧ ਵਿਦੇਸ਼ੀ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਹਰ ਸਾਲ 1,30,000 ਤੱਕ ਸੀਮਤ ਕਰਨਾ।

body: ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਸੈਨੇਟਰ ਹੈਨਸਨ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ, "ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਸਖ਼ਤ ਪਿਆਰ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਮੇਰਾ ਪਿਆਰ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆਈ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਲਈ ਹੈ।" ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਆਪਣੇ ਹੀ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਲਈ ਕਾਫ਼ੀ ਏਜਡ ਕੇਅਰ ਬੈੱਡ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੇ ਪਾ ਰਿਹਾ, ਅਤੇ ਜੋ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਮਾਪਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਥੇ ਲਿਆਉਣਾ ਚਾਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਨ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਖ਼ਰਚ ਆਪ ਚੁੱਕਣਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਅਤੇ ਜ਼ਿਆਦਾਤਰ ਸ਼ਰਨਾਰਥੀ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਕਰਨ ਨਾਲ ਦਸ ਸਾਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਸ 'ਤੇ ਖ਼ਰਚ 100 ਅਰਬ ਡਾਲਰ ਘਟੇਗਾ। ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਇਹ ਅੰਕੜਾ ਟ੍ਰੈਜ਼ਰੀ ਦੇ ਅੰਕੜਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਵਿਸ਼ਲੇਸ਼ਣ 'ਤੇ ਆਧਾਰਿਤ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਪਾਰਲੀਮੈਂਟਰੀ ਬਜਟ ਆਫ਼ਿਸ ਨੇ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਲਾਗਤ ਦਾ ਅੰਦਾਜ਼ਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਲਾਇਆ।

AAP ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਸੈਨੇਟਰ ਹੈਨਸਨ ਨੇ ਇਸ ਗੱਲ ਤੋਂ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ ਕਿ ਸ਼ਰਨਾਰਥੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਟੌਤੀ ਮੁਸਲਿਮ-ਬਹੁਗਿਣਤੀ ਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਜ਼ਿਆਦਾਤਰ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਸੀਰੀਆ, ਅਫ਼ਗ਼ਾਨਿਸਤਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਇਰਾਕ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਰਨਾਰਥੀਆਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।

body: ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਜਾਂ ਏਜਡ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਦੀ ਔਸਤ ਉਡੀਕ 42 ਸਾਲ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਕੰਟਰੀਬਿਊਟਰੀ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਦੀ 18 ਸਾਲ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਕਿਤੇ ਵੱਧ ਭੁਗਤਾਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

ul: ਲੇਬਰ: ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਵਿਦੇਸ਼ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਪੈਨੀ ਵੋਂਗ ਨੇ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਕਰਨ ਨੂੰ "ਬਹੁਤ ਕਠੋਰ" ਕਿਹਾ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਸ਼ਰਨਾਰਥੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਵੀਕਾਰ ਕਰਨਾ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਦਾ ਫ਼ਰਜ਼ ਹੈ। ਗ੍ਰਹਿ ਮਾਮਲਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਟੋਨੀ ਬਰਕ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਸ਼ੁੱਧ ਵਿਦੇਸ਼ੀ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਸ ਨੂੰ 2,25,000 ਤੱਕ ਲਿਆਉਣ ਦੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਟੀਚੇ 'ਤੇ ਕਾਇਮ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ AAP ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਚੇਤਾਵਨੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਕਿ ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਯੋਜਨਾਵਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਹੁਨਰਮੰਦ ਕਾਮੇ ਗੁਆ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਗੱਠਜੋੜ: AAP ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਸ਼ੈਡੋ ਖ਼ਜ਼ਾਨਚੀ ਟਿਮ ਵਿਲਸਨ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਸ ਬਾਰੇ ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ 'ਤੇ ਭਰੋਸਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ, ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਉਹ ਇੱਕ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਕਰਕੇ ਫਿਰ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਬਦਲ ਦਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ। ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਗੱਠਜੋੜ ਨੇ ਸ਼ਰਨਾਰਥੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਅੱਧੀ ਕਰਕੇ 10,000 ਕਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ੁੱਧ ਵਿਦੇਸ਼ੀ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਅੱਧੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਘਟਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਵਾਅਦਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ।

body: ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ 28 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਰਾਜ ਚੋਣਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਲੈ ਰਹੀ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਨਿਯਮ ਰਾਜ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸੰਘੀ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਤੈਅ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

body.note: ਇਸ ਐਲਾਨ ਨਾਲ ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਕਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਕੁਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਦਲਦਾ। ਜਦੋਂ ਤੱਕ ਸੰਘੀ ਸੰਸਦ ਨਿਯਮ ਨਾ ਬਦਲੇ, ਪੇਰੈਂਟ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਨਿਯਮ ਉਵੇਂ ਹੀ ਰਹਿਣਗੇ। ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਰਿਪੋਰਟ ਹੈ, ਪ੍ਰਵਾਸ ਸਲਾਹ ਨਹੀਂ: ਆਪਣੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਬਾਰੇ ਗ੍ਰਹਿ ਮਾਮਲਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਵਿਭਾਗ ਦੀ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ ਦੇਖੋ ਜਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਰਜਿਸਟਰਡ ਮਾਈਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਏਜੰਟ ਨਾਲ ਗੱਲ ਕਰੋ।

pa.dek: ਪੌਲੀਨ ਹੈਨਸਨ ਦਾ ਕਹਿਣਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਕਤਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਫ਼ੀਸ ਵਾਪਸ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਜਾਵੇਗੀ, ਅਤੇ ਜੋ ਮਾਪੇ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਇੱਥੇ ਹਨ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਣਾ ਪਵੇਗਾ, ਜਦੋਂ ਤੱਕ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਰਹਿਣ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਹੋਰ ਰਾਹ ਨਾ ਮਿਲੇ। ਪੈਨੀ ਵੋਂਗ ਨੇ ਇਸ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਨੂੰ 'ਬਹੁਤ ਕਠੋਰ' ਕਿਹਾ।

body: Australian wages grew at their fastest pace in almost three years in the September quarter, but not fast enough to keep up with the cost of living.

The Wage Price Index rose 1.1 per cent in the quarter and 3.5 per cent over the year, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) said on Wednesday. It was the strongest quarterly rise since the December quarter of 2023, and above the 3.4 per cent annual rise economists had expected, AAP reported.

Prices, though, rose 4.3 per cent in the 12 months to September, according to the ABS's consumer price index. The ABC reported it was the fourth quarter in a row in which wages had grown more slowly than inflation, which means the average pay packet buys less than it did a year ago.

ul: The minimum wage: ABS head of prices statistics Rachael McCririck said decisions by the Fair Work Commission, including the 4.75 per cent rise in award wages, were a key driver of private-sector wage growth this quarter.

Public sector pay: wages for government workers rose 1.3 per cent in the quarter and 3.9 per cent over the year, outpacing the private sector for the seventh quarter in a row. Ms McCririck said the main driver was pay rises for state government front-line workers such as nurses, midwives and police officers.
Private sector pay rose 1.0 per cent in the quarter and 3.4 per cent over the year.

Health care and social assistance made the largest contribution to growth this quarter, and accommodation and food services, where many workers are paid award rates, had the strongest quarterly rise, at 3.4 per cent.
34 per cent of jobs recorded an annualised pay rise of more than 4 per cent, up from 24 per cent a year earlier.

body: In original terms, Victorian wages rose 1.5 per cent in the quarter and 3.3 per cent over the year, the ABS said. New South Wales recorded 1.7 per cent and 3.5 per cent, driven by pay rises for its state government workers.

The pay rise comes as the job market cools. Unemployment rose from 4.4 per cent in June to 4.7 per cent in September, and job ads on Seek fell 6.4 per cent in the year to October while applications per ad reached a record high, AAP reported.
The Reserve Bank, which lifted the cash rate to 4.85 per cent in early November, watches wage growth closely because labour costs feed into the prices of services.

body.note: If you are paid under an award, check that your pay reflects this year's annual wage review with the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator, or call the Ombudsman on 13 13 94. International students and visa holders have the same workplace rights as other workers.

en.dek: Wages rose 1.1 per cent in the September quarter, lifted by the minimum wage increase, ABS figures show. But prices are rising faster, and Victorian pay grew more slowly than in New South Wales.

body: ऑस्ट्रेलियाई ब्यूरो ऑफ़ स्टैटिस्टिक्स (ABS) ने बुधवार को बताया कि वेज प्राइस इंडेक्स सितंबर तिमाही में 1.1 प्रतिशत और साल भर में 3.5 प्रतिशत बढ़ा। यह दिसंबर 2023 तिमाही के बाद सबसे बड़ी तिमाही वृद्धि है।

लेकिन ABS के उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकांक के अनुसार सितंबर तक के 12 महीनों में क़ीमतें 4.3 प्रतिशत बढ़ीं। ABC के अनुसार यह लगातार चौथी तिमाही है जब वेतन महंगाई से धीमा बढ़ा, यानी औसत तनख़्वाह से अब एक साल पहले से कम ख़रीदा जा सकता है।

ABS की रेचल मैक्क्रिरिक ने कहा कि फ़ेयर वर्क कमीशन के फ़ैसले, जिनमें अवॉर्ड वेतन में 4.75 प्रतिशत की बढ़ोतरी शामिल है, निजी क्षेत्र में वेतन वृद्धि की बड़ी वजह रहे। सरकारी कर्मचारियों का वेतन साल भर में 3.9 प्रतिशत और निजी क्षेत्र का 3.4 प्रतिशत बढ़ा।
विक्टोरिया में (मूल आँकड़ों में) वेतन तिमाही में 1.5 प्रतिशत और साल भर में 3.3 प्रतिशत बढ़ा, जबकि न्यू साउथ वेल्स में यह 1.7 और 3.5 प्रतिशत रहा।
AAP के अनुसार बेरोज़गारी जून में 4.4 प्रतिशत से बढ़कर सितंबर में 4.7 प्रतिशत हो गई, और Seek पर नौकरियों के विज्ञापन घटे, जबकि हर विज्ञापन पर आवेदन रिकॉर्ड स्तर पर पहुँच गए।

body.note: अगर आपको अवॉर्ड के तहत वेतन मिलता है, तो फ़ेयर वर्क ओम्बड्समैन के पे कैलकुलेटर से अपना वेतन जाँचें या 13 13 94 पर कॉल करें। अंतरराष्ट्रीय छात्रों और वीज़ा धारकों के कार्यस्थल अधिकार भी दूसरे कामगारों जैसे ही हैं।

hi.dek: ABS के आँकड़ों के अनुसार, न्यूनतम वेतन में बढ़ोतरी की वजह से सितंबर तिमाही में वेतन 1.1 प्रतिशत बढ़ा। लेकिन क़ीमतें इससे तेज़ बढ़ रही हैं, और विक्टोरिया में वेतन न्यू साउथ वेल्स से धीमा बढ़ा।

body: ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਅਨ ਬਿਊਰੋ ਆਫ਼ ਸਟੈਟਿਸਟਿਕਸ (ABS) ਨੇ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਵੇਜ ਪ੍ਰਾਈਸ ਇੰਡੈਕਸ ਸਤੰਬਰ ਤਿਮਾਹੀ ਵਿੱਚ 1.1 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਲ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ 3.5 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਵਧਿਆ। ਇਹ ਦਸੰਬਰ 2023 ਤਿਮਾਹੀ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਤਿਮਾਹੀ ਵਾਧਾ ਹੈ।

ਪਰ ABS ਦੇ ਖਪਤਕਾਰ ਮੁੱਲ ਸੂਚਕਾਂਕ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਸਤੰਬਰ ਤੱਕ ਦੇ 12 ਮਹੀਨਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੀਮਤਾਂ 4.3 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਵਧੀਆਂ। ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਇਹ ਲਗਾਤਾਰ ਚੌਥੀ ਤਿਮਾਹੀ ਹੈ ਜਦੋਂ ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹਾਂ ਮਹਿੰਗਾਈ ਨਾਲੋਂ ਹੌਲੀ ਵਧੀਆਂ, ਯਾਨੀ ਔਸਤ ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹ ਨਾਲ ਹੁਣ ਇੱਕ ਸਾਲ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਨਾਲੋਂ ਘੱਟ ਖ਼ਰੀਦਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

ABS ਦੀ ਰੇਚਲ ਮੈਕਕ੍ਰਿਰਿਕ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਫ਼ੇਅਰ ਵਰਕ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲੇ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਵਾਰਡ ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ 4.75 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਵਾਧਾ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹੈ, ਨਿੱਜੀ ਖੇਤਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹ ਵਾਧੇ ਦੀ ਵੱਡੀ ਵਜ੍ਹਾ ਰਹੇ। ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਮੁਲਾਜ਼ਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹ ਸਾਲ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ 3.9 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਅਤੇ ਨਿੱਜੀ ਖੇਤਰ ਦੀ 3.4 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਵਧੀ।
ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ (ਮੂਲ ਅੰਕੜਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ) ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹਾਂ ਤਿਮਾਹੀ ਵਿੱਚ 1.5 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਲ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ 3.3 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਵਧੀਆਂ, ਜਦਕਿ ਨਿਊ ਸਾਊਥ ਵੇਲਜ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਹ 1.7 ਅਤੇ 3.5 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਰਿਹਾ।
AAP ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਬੇਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰੀ ਜੂਨ ਵਿੱਚ 4.4 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਤੋਂ ਵਧ ਕੇ ਸਤੰਬਰ ਵਿੱਚ 4.7 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਹੋ ਗਈ, ਅਤੇ Seek 'ਤੇ ਨੌਕਰੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਇਸ਼ਤਿਹਾਰ ਘਟੇ, ਜਦਕਿ ਹਰ ਇਸ਼ਤਿਹਾਰ 'ਤੇ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਰਿਕਾਰਡ ਪੱਧਰ 'ਤੇ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਗਈਆਂ।

body.note: ਜੇ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਅਵਾਰਡ ਤਹਿਤ ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ, ਤਾਂ ਫ਼ੇਅਰ ਵਰਕ ਓਮਬਡਸਮੈਨ ਦੇ ਪੇ ਕੈਲਕੁਲੇਟਰ ਨਾਲ ਆਪਣੀ ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹ ਜਾਂਚੋ ਜਾਂ 13 13 94 'ਤੇ ਕਾਲ ਕਰੋ। ਕੌਮਾਂਤਰੀ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਧਾਰਕਾਂ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਵਾਲੀ ਥਾਂ ਦੇ ਹੱਕ ਵੀ ਹੋਰ ਕਾਮਿਆਂ ਵਾਂਗ ਹੀ ਹਨ।

body: England beat Australia by 97 runs in the third one-day international at Bellerive Oval in Hobart on Wednesday, winning the series 2-1 after losing the opening match in Perth.

Opener Ben Duckett made 133 from 115 balls, with 15 fours and three sixes, his third ODI century in five innings, cricket.com.au reported. Will Jacks added 59 from 48 balls as England were bowled out for 328.

Australia slumped to 3-34 early in the chase and were all out for 231 in the 47th over. Matt Renshaw made 55, his second half-century in a row, and also took 3-51 with his off-spin. Fast bowlers Jack Edwards (4-31) and Sonny Baker (4-45) did most of the damage for England.
"I've had success against Australia, but not in Australia. So it's nice," Duckett said, AAP reported.
Cameron Green retired hurt on 3 after a short ball from Gus Atkinson deflected off his arm onto the grille of his helmet, cricket.com.au reported. Oliver Peake came in to replace him and made 5.

The result ended a run of three straight 50-over series losses to Australia for England dating back to 2018. It was Australia's fourth ODI series loss this year by a 2-1 margin, after defeats by Pakistan, Bangladesh and South Africa, according to cricket.com.au. Australia will not play another one-day international until August next year.

body.note: Times are Melbourne time (AEDT), as listed by cricket.com.au. Check with the venue or Cricket Australia before you go.

en.dek: England came back from a heavy loss in Perth to win the one-day series 2-1. The two teams now play five T20 internationals, starting in Melbourne at 7.15pm on Saturday.
en.headline: Duckett century seals England's ODI series win in Hobart, with the T20s starting at the MCG on Saturday

ऑस्ट्रेलिया की टीम 47वें ओवर में 231 पर सिमट गई। मैट रेनशॉ ने 55 रन बनाए और 3 विकेट भी लिए। इंग्लैंड के जैक एडवर्ड्स ने 31 रन देकर 4 और सोनी बेकर ने 45 रन देकर 4 विकेट लिए। कैमरन ग्रीन गेंद लगने के बाद 3 रन पर रिटायर्ड हर्ट हुए।

body: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) is checking retailers across several sectors for misleading sales claims in the lead-up to Black Friday on 27 November and Cyber Monday on 30 November.

It is the watchdog's third sweep of the shopping events, and the first to look at promotions in emails and on social media as well as on retailers' websites, the ACCC said on Tuesday. Australians often spend close to $7 billion over the period, SBS News reported.

body.h: What the ACCC is looking for

ul: 'Sitewide' or 'storewide' sales where many products are excluded
Time-limited offers and countdown timers that keep running after the stated end date
Pressure tactics, such as misleading testimonials or false claims that stock is about to run out
Sale prices compared against a 'was' price the product was never, or not recently, sold at

body: "Retailers risk ACCC enforcement action if they misrepresent the size, scope or duration of their sales," ACCC deputy chair Catriona Lowe said. "Retailers should not be relying on fine print disclaimers or exclusions to qualify the headline message of a promotion."

Earlier sweeps led to penalties. Michael Hill, My House and Hairhouse Warehouse Online paid penalties in June 2025 over alleged misleading sitewide claims, and digiDirect, James Lane and Vuly paid penalties in September this year, the ACCC said.

In the first nine months of 2026, 58.7 per cent of Scamwatch reports involving a financial loss were about buying and selling scams, the ACCC said. It warned shoppers to be wary of fake online shops that use big discounts and 'limited time' pressure to rush people into paying.

ul: Focus on the final price you will pay, not the promotional headline
Read the exclusions and conditions before you buy
Compare prices across retailers and against the product's past prices
Buy only if the price and timing suit you, not because a timer is counting down
Check you are dealing with a legitimate seller

body: "Consumers should be aware that a 'sale' sign doesn't always mean it's a good deal," Ms Lowe said.

body.note: To report a misleading sale, use the ACCC's consumer issue form at accc.gov.au. Report scams to Scamwatch.

en.dek: The consumer watchdog's third Black Friday sweep will, for the first time, check retailers' emails and social media as well as their websites. Here is what it is looking for, and how to shop safely.
en.headline: Black Friday sales: the ACCC is watching for fake 'storewide' deals and countdown timers

body: AI companies could face criminal prosecution in Australia if their systems cause harm and they have not taken reasonable steps to prevent it, under an option the federal government is now considering.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the government's response on Tuesday to a review of an incident in which an AI agent made by OpenAI accessed a Medicare statistics website, the ABC and SBS reported.

SBS reported that the government had accepted all 18 recommendations of the rapid review. They include new mandatory safeguards for AI companies operating in Australia, an AI safety regulator to enforce them, mandatory reporting of AI security breaches and of potential breaches of criminal law, and independent evaluation of the most advanced AI models.

According to the ABC, one recommendation was to consider options to reform the criminal law to improve AI safety, and another was to consider criminal penalties for egregious breaches of AI safety standards. The ABC reported the government says the new offence would make Australia the first country to prosecute AI companies on this basis, and that the regulator could issue significant fines. No fine amounts have been given.
SBS reported that the AI agent accessed the Medicare statistics website in June, and that OpenAI informed federal authorities in September.

The ABC reported that a letter from the Australian Federal Police to a parliamentary inquiry, released last week, said the AFP had received no formal report of a crime and had not opened a criminal investigation. Mr Albanese did not say whether he believed OpenAI had committed a crime, and described the hack as "minor in terms of direct implications".

"Australia is a first mover in this space, and we want to make sure that we reap the potential benefits of AI," Mr Albanese told reporters in Canberra, SBS reported. "But we need to ensure that we get it right, and social licence is absolutely critical."
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told the ABC: "It should never be the case that there's an argument that someone didn't know the computer was loaded."

body.h: Experts question how it would work

body: Legal experts quoted by the ABC were cautious. Monash University associate professor Michael Duffy pointed to "problems of proof, working out if harms were foreseeable and proving fault". UTS industry professor Ed Santow said: "I think what will be much more useful is the civil one."
The ABC reported that Italy already has a criminal offence for high-risk AI uses that lack required safeguards, but no one has been prosecuted under it.
OpenAI told the ABC it was reviewing the proposals. The government's AI standards are expected by the end of the year, the ABC reported.

body.note: The Melbourne Indian uses AI tools, including Anthropic's Claude, to help research and draft stories. Anthropic was one of the AI companies the ABC contacted for comment; the ABC reported it did not respond.

en.dek: The federal government says it has accepted every recommendation of a review into the OpenAI incident, and is considering what it calls a world-first offence for AI companies.
en.headline: AI companies could face criminal charges in Australia after an AI agent breached a Medicare website

body: A serious form of alcohol-related liver disease is sending younger Victorians and a growing number of women to hospital, according to a new report released on Thursday.

The report, by the Burnet Institute and commissioned by the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education (FARE), looked at Victorian hospital admissions for alcohol-associated hepatitis, a severe inflammation of the liver, from 2017 to mid-2024.

ul: About 40 per cent of people admitted to hospital with alcohol-associated hepatitis were under their mid-40s.
Women now make up about one in three cases.
Admissions rose sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic and remain above pre-pandemic levels. FARE says male admissions are more than double their pre-COVID rate.
The ABC reported that about 13 per cent of patients needed intensive care and the condition had a 4 per cent mortality rate.

body: Professor Jessica Howell, who leads the Burnet Institute's hepatitis and liver cancer research group and is a gastroenterologist at St Vincent's Hospital, said in FARE's release that "women are catching up to men in terms of liver-related harms from alcohol".
She told the ABC the liver can recover if drinking stops early: "We know that the liver can regenerate very well."
FARE chief executive Ayla Chorley said: "This data tells us that reducing alcohol use significantly reduces harm."

ul: Australia's guidelines recommend no more than 10 standard drinks a week and no more than four on any one day.
If you are worried about your own or a family member's drinking, start with your GP.
DirectLine (1800 888 236) offers free, confidential alcohol and drug counselling in Victoria, 24 hours a day. For an interpreter, call TIS National on 131 450.

body.note: This is general health information. Speak to a doctor about your own situation.

en.dek: A Burnet Institute report for the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education found about four in ten hospital admissions for alcohol-associated hepatitis were people under their mid-40s.
en.headline: Severe alcohol-related liver disease is hitting younger Victorians and more women, report finds

body: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has taken the Commonwealth Bank to the Federal Court, alleging it overcharged about 42,000 business customers roughly $8.5 million in fees they were not told about.
The civil penalty case was filed late on Wednesday and concerns CommBiz, CBA's online banking platform for businesses, according to reports by the ABC and AAP.

ASIC says the CommBiz terms and conditions told customers they would pay a fee for direct debit and direct credit payments to or from a third party's account. It alleges CBA also charged a second fee, which was not disclosed, for the matching movement of money into or out of the customer's own CommBiz account.
The ABC reported ASIC's example: a business paying wages to 10 employees from two accounts was charged 12 fees, two of them undisclosed.

The case covers fees charged between November 2020 and May 2025. But ASIC alleges the misleading terms had been in place for about 19 years, since CommBiz launched in 2006, that the bank received complaints about the fees from at least 2015, and that a 2016 internal audit found direct debit fees were being overcharged.
"We allege Commonwealth Bank broke a basic promise to its business customers," ASIC commissioner Alan Kirkland said. "Small businesses are busy enough."
ASIC is seeking declarations, financial penalties, adverse publicity orders and costs. The court has not yet set a date for the first hearing.

In a statement to the ASX reported by the ABC, CBA said it had identified the problem itself, reported it to ASIC and cooperated fully. It said the issue came from simplified terms that did not accurately describe how the fee, 25 cents plus GST, was charged. The bank said it "accepts that it did not get things right for CommBiz customers" and apologised, but disputes how some allegations are framed. It said it would defend parts of the claim or keep working with ASIC to resolve it.

CBA stopped charging the fees in June 2025 and changed the terms that August. It says a remediation program covering December 2006 onwards has already paid more than $26.4 million to about 93,000 customers, including about 40,000 small businesses.

ul: CBA says its remediation program is complete. If you think you were affected and have not heard from the bank, contact CBA directly.
If you are not satisfied with the bank's answer, the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) handles complaints from small businesses for free: afca.org.au or 1800 931 678.

body.note: These are allegations made by ASIC in civil proceedings. They have not been tested in court.

en.dek: The corporate regulator says CBA's CommBiz terms did not disclose a second fee on direct debits and credits. The bank says it found the problem itself and has already repaid more than $26 million.
en.headline: ASIC sues Commonwealth Bank, alleging it overcharged 42,000 business customers $8.5 million in hidden fees

body: People applying for an Australian visa in India may now be asked to provide biometrics, meaning fingerprints and a facial image, as part of the application. The Australian High Commission in New Delhi announced the change from 26 October 2026.

The High Commission says India is one of nearly 60 countries where Australia is expanding biometric collection. The rule applies only to new applications lodged from 26 October; applications already submitted are not affected.
This matters for Melbourne families sponsoring or inviting parents, relatives and friends from India, such as for visitor visas.

ul: The Department of Home Affairs tells each applicant whether they need to provide biometrics, with instructions.
Depending on their circumstances, applicants may be asked to attend an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre in person.
Eligible applicants who have given biometrics at a collection centre before and hold a valid passport may be able to use the Australian Immi App instead, at no cost.
The High Commission says visa processing times are not expected to be affected.

body: The announcement does not list which visa types or age groups are covered. Applicants should follow the instructions they receive from Home Affairs.

body.note: This is general information, not migration advice. Check the Department of Home Affairs biometrics page or speak to a registered migration agent about your situation.

body: भारत में ऑस्ट्रेलियाई वीज़ा के लिए आवेदन करने वालों से अब आवेदन के हिस्से के रूप में बायोमेट्रिक्स, यानी उंगलियों के निशान और चेहरे की तस्वीर, माँगी जा सकती है। नई दिल्ली स्थित ऑस्ट्रेलियाई हाई कमीशन ने 26 अक्टूबर 2026 से इस बदलाव की घोषणा की।

हाई कमीशन का कहना है कि भारत उन लगभग 60 देशों में से एक है जहाँ ऑस्ट्रेलिया बायोमेट्रिक्स लेने का दायरा बढ़ा रहा है। यह नियम सिर्फ़ 26 अक्टूबर से जमा किए गए नए आवेदनों पर लागू होता है; पहले से जमा आवेदनों पर कोई असर नहीं पड़ेगा।
यह मेलबर्न के उन परिवारों के लिए अहम है जो भारत से माता-पिता, रिश्तेदारों और दोस्तों को स्पॉन्सर करते हैं या बुलाते हैं, जैसे विज़िटर वीज़ा के लिए।

ul: Department of Home Affairs हर आवेदक को बताता है कि उसे बायोमेट्रिक्स देने हैं या नहीं, और साथ में निर्देश भी देता है।
परिस्थितियों के अनुसार आवेदकों को किसी ऑस्ट्रेलियन बायोमेट्रिक्स कलेक्शन सेंटर पर ख़ुद जाने के लिए कहा जा सकता है।
जो योग्य आवेदक पहले किसी कलेक्शन सेंटर पर बायोमेट्रिक्स दे चुके हैं और जिनके पास मान्य पासपोर्ट है, वे इसके बजाय बिना किसी ख़र्च के Australian Immi App का इस्तेमाल कर सकते हैं।
हाई कमीशन का कहना है कि इससे वीज़ा प्रोसेसिंग के समय पर असर पड़ने की उम्मीद नहीं है।

body: घोषणा में यह नहीं बताया गया है कि कौन-से वीज़ा प्रकार या आयु वर्ग इसमें शामिल हैं। आवेदकों को Home Affairs से मिलने वाले निर्देशों का पालन करना चाहिए।

body.note: यह सामान्य जानकारी है, माइग्रेशन सलाह नहीं। अपनी स्थिति के बारे में Department of Home Affairs का बायोमेट्रिक्स पेज देखें या किसी पंजीकृत माइग्रेशन एजेंट से बात करें।

body: ਭਾਰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆਈ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਲਈ ਅਪਲਾਈ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਹੁਣ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਹਿੱਸੇ ਵਜੋਂ ਬਾਇਓਮੈਟ੍ਰਿਕਸ, ਯਾਨੀ ਉਂਗਲਾਂ ਦੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਚਿਹਰੇ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ, ਮੰਗੀ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ। ਨਵੀਂ ਦਿੱਲੀ ਸਥਿਤ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆਈ ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਨੇ 26 ਅਕਤੂਬਰ 2026 ਤੋਂ ਇਸ ਤਬਦੀਲੀ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ।

ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਦਾ ਕਹਿਣਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਭਾਰਤ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਤਕਰੀਬਨ 60 ਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਹੈ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਬਾਇਓਮੈਟ੍ਰਿਕਸ ਲੈਣ ਦਾ ਦਾਇਰਾ ਵਧਾ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਨਿਯਮ ਸਿਰਫ਼ 26 ਅਕਤੂਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ ਨਵੀਆਂ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਲਾਗੂ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ; ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਕੋਈ ਅਸਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਵੇਗਾ।
ਇਹ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਅਹਿਮ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਭਾਰਤ ਤੋਂ ਮਾਪਿਆਂ, ਰਿਸ਼ਤੇਦਾਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਦੋਸਤਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਪਾਂਸਰ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ ਜਾਂ ਸੱਦਦੇ ਹਨ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਵਿਜ਼ਿਟਰ ਵੀਜ਼ੇ ਲਈ।

ul: Department of Home Affairs ਹਰ ਬਿਨੈਕਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਬਾਇਓਮੈਟ੍ਰਿਕਸ ਦੇਣੇ ਹਨ ਜਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ, ਅਤੇ ਨਾਲ ਹਦਾਇਤਾਂ ਵੀ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
ਹਾਲਾਤ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਬਿਨੈਕਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਅਨ ਬਾਇਓਮੈਟ੍ਰਿਕਸ ਕਲੈਕਸ਼ਨ ਸੈਂਟਰ 'ਤੇ ਖ਼ੁਦ ਜਾਣ ਲਈ ਕਿਹਾ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
ਜਿਹੜੇ ਯੋਗ ਬਿਨੈਕਾਰ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਕਲੈਕਸ਼ਨ ਸੈਂਟਰ 'ਤੇ ਬਾਇਓਮੈਟ੍ਰਿਕਸ ਦੇ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਕੋਲ ਯੋਗ ਪਾਸਪੋਰਟ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਖ਼ਰਚੇ ਦੇ Australian Immi App ਵਰਤ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ।
ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਦਾ ਕਹਿਣਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਪ੍ਰੋਸੈਸਿੰਗ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ 'ਤੇ ਅਸਰ ਪੈਣ ਦੀ ਉਮੀਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।

body: ਐਲਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਕਿ ਕਿਹੜੀਆਂ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਕਿਸਮਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਉਮਰ ਵਰਗ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹਨ। ਬਿਨੈਕਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ Home Affairs ਤੋਂ ਮਿਲਣ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਹਦਾਇਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਕਰਨੀ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।

body.note: ਇਹ ਆਮ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਹੈ, ਮਾਈਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਸਲਾਹ ਨਹੀਂ। ਆਪਣੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਬਾਰੇ Department of Home Affairs ਦਾ ਬਾਇਓਮੈਟ੍ਰਿਕਸ ਪੰਨਾ ਦੇਖੋ ਜਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਰਜਿਸਟਰਡ ਮਾਈਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਏਜੰਟ ਨਾਲ ਗੱਲ ਕਰੋ।

body: Westpac is lending to 30 per cent fewer housing construction projects than it was up to a year and a half ago, its chief executive Anthony Miller has told a parliamentary inquiry.

Mr Miller and ANZ chief executive Nuno Matos gave evidence in Canberra on Thursday to the inquiry into the big four banks, chaired by Labor MP Ed Husic. The Commonwealth Bank and NAB are scheduled to appear on Friday, AAP reported.

Mr Miller put the fall in construction lending mainly down to rising costs rather than the federal government's May budget changes, which abolished negative gearing and the capital gains tax discount, with a carve-out for new builds. Each dollar was "delivering fewer houses", he said, according to AAP.
He said the carve-out for new builds was helping, but slowly: "There is some improvement in that area, but it has not come through as fast or as significant as perhaps we would like."

"Providing more resource for the demand side isn't going to solve the problem," Mr Miller said. He said higher building costs and slow approvals were pushing developers towards more expensive homes, and gave an example: a builder might make a 10 per cent margin on 15 apartments but 30 per cent on three. "What we need is more affordable housing," he said.

Mr Husic said the banks earn close to $300,000 from an average 30-year owner-occupier loan, up $40,000 since interest rates began rising this year, SBS News reported. Mr Matos disputed the figures and said mortgages are among the least profitable parts of banking.

Mr Matos told the inquiry ANZ expects home prices to fall about 13.5 per cent from peak to trough and to stabilise in 2028, according to SBS. He said the share of ANZ customers in hardship had risen to five in 1,000, and that ANZ's loan applications had fallen 12 per cent in six months, with investor applications down 27 per cent.

Asked about artificial intelligence, Mr Matos said AI was not behind ANZ's recently completed program to cut 3,500 jobs, but could not guarantee there would be no future job losses from technology, AAP reported.
The hearings come a day after figures showed investor home loans fell a record 30.6 per cent in the year to September.

body: Councillor Abhishek Awasthi has been elected Mayor of the City of Greater Bendigo for 2026-27, the council announced this week.
Councillors chose Cr Awasthi at a meeting at Bendigo's Capital Theatre on Monday night. Cr Andrea Metcalf was elected Deputy Mayor. They replace Cr Thomas Prince and Cr Karen Corr.
The Indian Sun reported that Cr Awasthi is the first person of Indian origin to be mayor of Greater Bendigo. He was deputy mayor in 2024-25, serving alongside Cr Metcalf when she was mayor.

Cr Awasthi represents Kennington Ward and was first elected to council in November 2024. According to his council profile, he has lived in Greater Bendigo since 2010, lives in Kennington with his wife and daughter, and volunteers with the CFA's Bendigo Fire Brigade.

The Indian Sun reported that he is originally from Mandi in Himachal Pradesh, came to Australia in 2008 to study biotechnology at La Trobe University, and became an Australian citizen in 2015. It said his parents and relatives attended the meeting.

In the council's announcement, Cr Awasthi said he was honoured by his colleagues' confidence. "Listening to our community will remain at the heart of my approach," he said, adding: "Small businesses are the lifeblood of our local economy."
His council profile lists his priorities as strong governance, economic development and building partnerships across the community.
Cr Metcalf said affordable housing, community partnerships, active transport and tackling illegal dumping were among her priorities.
en.dek: The Kennington Ward councillor, who came to Australia from Himachal Pradesh to study, will lead the regional city for the next year. The Indian Sun reports he is its first mayor of Indian origin.

body: पार्षद अभिषेक अवस्थी को 2026-27 के लिए सिटी ऑफ़ ग्रेटर बेंडिगो का मेयर चुना गया है। सोमवार रात कैपिटल थिएटर में हुई बैठक में पार्षदों ने उन्हें चुना। पार्षद एंड्रिया मेटकाफ़ उप-मेयर बनीं।
द इंडियन सन के अनुसार वे ग्रेटर बेंडिगो के पहले भारतीय मूल के मेयर हैं। वे 2024-25 में उप-मेयर रह चुके हैं।

काउंसिल के अनुसार वे 2010 से ग्रेटर बेंडिगो में रहते हैं और CFA की बेंडिगो फ़ायर ब्रिगेड में स्वयंसेवक हैं। द इंडियन सन के अनुसार वे हिमाचल प्रदेश के मंडी से हैं और 2008 में ला ट्रोब विश्वविद्यालय में पढ़ने आए थे।
काउंसिल की घोषणा में उन्होंने कहा कि समुदाय की बात सुनना उनके काम का केंद्र रहेगा और छोटे व्यवसाय स्थानीय अर्थव्यवस्था की जीवनरेखा हैं।

body: ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਅਭਿਸ਼ੇਕ ਅਵਸਥੀ ਨੂੰ 2026-27 ਲਈ ਸਿਟੀ ਆਫ਼ ਗ੍ਰੇਟਰ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਦਾ ਮੇਅਰ ਚੁਣਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਸੋਮਵਾਰ ਰਾਤ ਕੈਪੀਟਲ ਥੀਏਟਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੋਈ ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੌਂਸਲਰਾਂ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਚੁਣਿਆ। ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਐਂਡਰੀਆ ਮੈਟਕਾਫ਼ ਡਿਪਟੀ ਮੇਅਰ ਬਣੇ।
ਦ ਇੰਡੀਅਨ ਸਨ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਹ ਗ੍ਰੇਟਰ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਦੇ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਮੂਲ ਦੇ ਮੇਅਰ ਹਨ। ਉਹ 2024-25 ਵਿੱਚ ਡਿਪਟੀ ਮੇਅਰ ਰਹਿ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ।

ਕੌਂਸਲ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਹ 2010 ਤੋਂ ਗ੍ਰੇਟਰ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ CFA ਦੀ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਫ਼ਾਇਰ ਬ੍ਰਿਗੇਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਲੰਟੀਅਰ ਹਨ। ਦ ਇੰਡੀਅਨ ਸਨ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਹ ਹਿਮਾਚਲ ਪ੍ਰਦੇਸ਼ ਦੇ ਮੰਡੀ ਤੋਂ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ 2008 ਵਿੱਚ ਲਾ ਟ੍ਰੋਬ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੜ੍ਹਨ ਆਏ ਸਨ।

body: A former CFMEU organiser has told Victoria's Big Build royal commission that underworld figure Mick Gatto gave him an expensive gold bracelet, and that Mr Gatto sometimes intervened with the union on behalf of employers.
Paul Tzimas, who worked full-time as a union organiser, gave evidence on Wednesday, the third day of public hearings. AAP and NCA NewsWire both reported his evidence.

Mr Tzimas said he first refused the gift, then accepted it after Mr Gatto called it an "olive branch" and said he wanted nothing in return. He said he never wore it. "He never called upon any favours," Mr Tzimas told the commission, according to NCA NewsWire.
Asked by counsel assisting Chris Carr SC whether Mr Gatto would intervene with the union for employers, Mr Tzimas agreed.

Mr Carr put a list of names to the witness. Mr Tzimas identified 11 CFMEU organisers and health and safety representatives who, AAP reported, were affiliated with outlaw motorcycle gangs at the time or previously, and agreed the union had placed them on building sites.
He also agreed the union pushed hard to get its way, which he said was "to deliver outcomes for working people". He admitted breaking the law several times as an organiser and said he had been fined.

The first fortnight of hearings is focused on a two-day stoppage at the Gap Road level crossing removal in Sunbury in June 2022, when union delegates occupied the site and work resumed only after their demands were agreed.

WorkSafe inspector Quinton Drury told the commission the stoppage was given the lowest priority because priority is set by safety risk, not by disruption to projects. Inspectors arrived on 8 June 2022, after the dispute was resolved, and found only "minor" issues with piling holes, which were fixed during the inspection, AAP reported.

The royal commission is examining the integrity of the state's Big Build infrastructure program. Its hearings are running through the campaign for the 28 November state election, and its final report is due in August 2027. Witnesses are legally compelled to attend, and counsel assisting Chris Young KC has warned that threatening or intimidating a witness is a serious criminal offence.

body.note: Evidence given to a royal commission has not been tested in court. No finding has been made against anyone named.

en.dek: On the third day of hearings, a former organiser told the royal commission that the underworld figure sometimes stepped in for employers, and that WorkSafe gave the Sunbury site occupation its lowest priority.

body: The royal commission into corruption on Victoria's major infrastructure projects has heard that a two-day union stoppage at a Sunbury level crossing site in 2022 pushed up the project's costs by an estimated $6 million, and that the state paid for it.

"Practically speaking, every dollar spent at Gap Road was paid first by the state," counsel assisting Chris Young KC told the hearing in Collingwood on Monday, according to ABC News coverage. The first witnesses are due to give evidence from today, Tuesday 10 November.

body.note: Allegations aired at a royal commission are not proven. Mr Young said some of them have been denied. The commission has made no findings.

body.h: What the commission heard on day one

body: Mr Young said union officials repeatedly ordered work to stop on 6 and 7 June 2022, during a shutdown of the Sunbury line for critical works. Work resumed that evening after a meeting at the CFMEU's offices, without the safety issues that had been cited being fixed, he said. Union-backed health and safety representatives were appointed shortly afterwards.

A labour-hire firm engaged on the site in June 2022 went from two workers to 20 and billed about $1.2 million by September, the commission heard. That firm's licence has since been cancelled. CFMEU officials visited the site 34 times in a year, while WorkSafe inspectors recorded no breaches, Mr Young said.

The project's target cost rose from $110 million to $116 million after the stoppage. It was delivered for $104 million, which Mr Young said meant the alliance building it collected about $2 million in extra profit under its contract. He said other contractors had described "remarkably similar" experiences on other major projects, including North East Link, and that some agencies had been slow to hand over documents.

The hearing was also read a 2017 memo by contractor John Holland which said the CFMEU had "unprecedented access to ministers" and would probably know about government tenders before they were announced. Notes from a contractors' meeting recorded a threat that workers would be "smashed" if they turned up. Police and WorkSafe were notified, the commission heard, but no action was taken. These are claims recorded in documents, not findings.

Premier Ben Carroll denied knowing about the CFMEU's access to senior officials and ministers. "What today's hearings show is that I am a premier that will make the tough decisions," he said. He also confirmed the state would pay for lawyers for former premiers Jacinta Allan and Daniel Andrews at the inquiry. "I want to make sure Victorians get the answers they deserve," he said.

body.h: What the commission will look at

body: Mr Young set out themes the inquiry expects to explore. They include allegations that the union placed unelected delegates on sites as health and safety representatives, sometimes through labour-hire companies, and that contractors were often left to deal with disruption themselves by "buying peace" and pricing its cost into their bids. He said those costs were shared with the state or passed on to it.

He tendered a June 2023 briefing to Jacinta Allan, then the transport infrastructure minister, which raised concerns including pressure on contractors, excess staffing on sites, a rise in full-time union delegates and threats of unprotected industrial action. The briefing records concerns raised at the time and is not a finding. AAP has reported that Ms Allan, who later became premier, will be required to give evidence, but it is not yet known when.
Later hearing blocks will examine alleged links between organised crime and the construction industry, and how government money was allocated and projects chosen.
Mr Young also warned that threatening or punishing a witness is a serious offence, and said any reported threat would be referred to Victoria Police.

The Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria was established on 20 August 2026. It is led by the Honourable Christopher Kourakis AC, a former chief justice of South Australia, and its final report is due by 20 August 2027.

Premier Ben Carroll called the inquiry as his first act after replacing Ms Allan, who had resisted calls from across the parliament for a royal commission. The calls followed reporting by Nine newspapers in 2024 alleging corruption and criminal infiltration of the CFMEU and Big Build sites. Parts of the union were placed into administration by the federal government in August 2024.

A report for the union's administrators by barrister Geoffrey Watson SC estimated that alleged corrupt conduct had effectively cost Victorian taxpayers $15 billion. That figure is Mr Watson's estimate, and testing claims like it is part of the commission's work.

This block of hearings runs until Friday 20 November, overlapping with early voting, which opens on Wednesday 18 November. Polling day is Saturday 28 November. A second block of hearings is expected before the end of the year, ABC News has reported.
ABC News has reported that the hearings will run through about two weeks of the four-week campaign. Mr Carroll has said that "integrity is not negotiable".

body: The commission also takes submissions from anyone with information relevant to its terms of reference, through its website.

body: The first witnesses at Victoria's Big Build royal commission on Tuesday described how CFMEU officials halted work on a rail project in Sunbury, in Melbourne's north-west, in June 2022, according to reports from AAP and NCA NewsWire.
On Monday, counsel assisting told the commission that the Gap Road level-crossing removal came under the union's control in June 2022. Tuesday's evidence came from people who were on that site.

Crane operator Glenn Tyrrell, who was on the job through a labour-hire company and was the site's elected health and safety representative, said work had been going well with no union presence until early June 2022, when the project entered a 30-day rail shutdown.

He told the commission officials came on site and stopped the cranes and much of the work. "They just stopped works," he said, according to both reports. He said he did not think the officials were allowed to enter.

After work resumed, Mr Tyrrell said, he was told he would now be employed through a different labour-hire firm, BK Labour, and asked by counsel whether he joined the union, he replied: "Had to." NCA NewsWire reported that he paid about $1,200 that year and that his pay rate did not change.

ul: A John Holland supervisor on the project, Robert Van Den Tol, gave evidence of 56 union visits under right-of-entry notices between late January and late June 2022, NCA NewsWire reported. Under questioning from the CFMEU's lawyer, he agreed a WorkSafe note about protection around 11-metre-deep holes appeared to be a valid complaint.
AAP reported that the traffic-control contractor on site was replaced four days after a closed-door meeting during the stoppage, with workers under the new firm paid roughly double.
A July 2022 briefing to then transport minister Jacinta Allan warned that a CFMEU campaign for higher traffic-management pay would cost the state an extra $400 million, AAP reported.
Minutes of a meeting during the stoppage, put to the commission, recorded threats allegedly made to workers of another contractor.

body: The evidence is untested and the commission has made no findings. Neither report included a response from the CFMEU, which is represented at the hearing.
The commission, set up by Premier Ben Carroll's government in August, is hearing evidence during the state election campaign. Victorians vote on 28 November.

body: Two days into its first public hearings, Victoria's royal commission into corruption on major construction projects has looked at just one job: the removal of a level crossing at Gap Road, Sunbury, in 2022. But the documents and evidence aired in a Collingwood hearing room this week reach well beyond one rail bridge, to the questions of how much power the CFMEU held on Big Build sites, what that cost taxpayers, and how much the state knew.

None of it has been tested. The commission has made no findings, some of the allegations have been denied, and the union is represented at the hearing and has questioned witnesses. This block of hearings runs until Friday 20 November, two days after early voting opens, so the first early voters will cast their ballots while evidence is still being heard, and long before any findings are made.

body.note: Allegations and evidence at a royal commission are not proven. Documents read at the hearing record what their authors believed at the time. The commission's final report is not due until August 2027.

body.h: Five things the commission has heard

ul: One job, two days, $6 million. Counsel assisting Chris Young KC said a stoppage on 6 and 7 June 2022 pushed Gap Road's target cost from $110 million to $116 million, and that "every dollar" spent on the site was paid first by the state, according to ABC News. The project was eventually delivered for $104 million, which he said meant the alliance building it collected about $2 million in extra profit under its contract.

A worker says he 'had to' join. Crane operator Glenn Tyrrell, the site's elected health and safety representative, told the commission that union organisers would "come on site and literally stop the whole job", ABC News reported. He said about 15 casual workers were later called into a lunch room, told to move to a different labour-hire firm and told they had to join the CFMEU. He said he paid $590 up front for six months of union fees, the first time he had joined any union.

Safety was the stated reason, and the supervisor disputes it. John Holland site supervisor Robert Van Den Tol, giving evidence by video, said he had always considered the site safe and rejected the union's claim of a risk-assessment problem with piling work: "if I had seen it, I would have stopped it," he said, according to ABC News. He said he believed the union was targeting the project because it was the last crew in Melbourne without a union-affiliated safety representative. Under questioning from the CFMEU's lawyer, he agreed that a WorkSafe note about protection around deep holes appeared to be a valid complaint, NCA NewsWire reported.

The costs spread beyond one site. AAP reported that the site's traffic-control contractor was replaced four days after a closed-door meeting during the stoppage. The Guardian reported counsel as saying traffic controllers' rates rose from about $45 to $88 an hour, and that a government briefing to Jacinta Allan, then the minister responsible, estimated the union's campaign over traffic-management pay would add $60 million to $78 million to current projects and well over $400 million to projects being planned.

The paper trail reaches government. Internal documents from the contractor John Holland, read at the hearing, described the CFMEU as having "unprecedented access to ministers" and "a significant level of influence within the state government", AAP and The Guardian reported. These are a contractor's views, not findings. Counsel also tendered a June 2023 briefing to Ms Allan that raised concerns about pressure on contractors, excess staffing and a rise in full-time union delegates.

body.h: Gap Road, June 2022: the timeline so far

dl: The CFMEU issues eight safety notices to John Holland, ABC News reported. A further 23 notices follow on 1 and 2 June.
The project enters a planned 30-day shutdown of the Sunbury line.
Union officials stop work on the site.
A meeting is held at the CFMEU's offices. Work resumes afterwards, without the safety issues that had been cited being fixed, counsel said.
The traffic-control contractor is replaced (AAP). About a week after the stoppage, casual workers are told to change labour-hire firm and join the union (Mr Tyrrell's evidence).
Works are completed. The project comes in at $104 million against a revised target of $116 million.

body.h: What the union and the politicians say

body: The CFMEU's construction division has been in administration since the federal government intervened in August 2024. Its lawyers have cross-examined witnesses this week, but none of the reports we read carried a public response from the union or its administrators to the evidence. Administrator Michael Crosby has previously said developers, head contractors, subcontractors and labour-hire operators should also be called, ABC News reported.

The commission's own terms of reference exclude lawful industrial action and lawful actions under workplace safety laws. The question for the commissioner is whether conduct went beyond what the law allows.

Premier Ben Carroll, who announced the inquiry on the day he replaced Ms Allan as Labor leader in July, has said Victorians "deserve answers". His government is paying for lawyers for Ms Allan and former premier Daniel Andrews. Liberal leader Jess Wilson said that "doesn't pass the pub test", The Guardian reported.

Lawyers for Ms Allan and Mr Andrews attended Monday's hearing, and both are open to being called to give evidence, AAP reported. Counsel assisting has said notices will be issued to each person named in the 2023 briefing "in due course", The Nightly reported. No date has been announced.

body.h: The questions still to be answered

ul: How much did the state know? "We will examine how much the state knew and what it didn't," Commissioner Christopher Kourakis said on Monday, according to AAP.
Was Gap Road typical? Counsel said other contractors had described "remarkably similar" experiences on other major projects, including North East Link, ABC News reported.

Where does organised crime fit in? Counsel said apparently legitimate businesses had paid people linked to organised crime for services that appeared to involve "little more than intimidation and menace", AAP reported. Later hearing blocks will examine those links, and how government money was allocated and projects chosen.

Is anyone holding back? Counsel said some parties had not complied with notices to produce documents, in some cases citing government policy, The Guardian reported. He also said about half of the companies invited to make voluntary submissions had not responded, NCA NewsWire reported.

What did it all cost? A report for the union's administrators by barrister Geoffrey Watson SC estimated that alleged corrupt conduct had effectively cost Victorian taxpayers $15 billion. That is his estimate, and testing claims like it is part of the commission's job.

body.h: No Tests in Mumbai, Kolkata or Bengaluru

body: India's cricket board announced the venues in March. None of the five Tests is in Kolkata, Mumbai or Bengaluru, three established Test grounds that have long drawn big crowds, AAP reported.

Guwahati's stadium staged its first Test in November 2025, against South Africa. Ahmedabad, which hosts the final Test, has become India's ground of choice for major matches, including the 2023 ODI World Cup final and the 2026 T20 World Cup final.
Australia arrive as holders, after winning the last series 3-1 at home.
India's home summer leads into the series: three ODIs and three T20 Internationals against Sri Lanka from 13 to 27 December, and three ODIs against Zimbabwe from 3 to 9 January.
Australia have a busy run beforehand, with a four-Test home series against New Zealand that includes the Boxing Day Test at the MCG from 26 December.

body: Workers earning about $45,000 a year, and those approaching the top tax bracket, stand to lose the biggest share of future pay rises to 'bracket creep', according to research released on Wednesday by the e61 Institute, an independent economic research centre.
Bracket creep happens because income tax thresholds are not adjusted for inflation. As wages rise, more of each dollar is taxed at higher rates, even when a pay rise only keeps up with prices.

The research note, by Michael Brennan, Richard Holden, Greg Kaplan, Matthew Maltman and Matt Nolan, models the decade from 2027–28 on the assumption that there are no further income tax cuts. It includes changes already legislated.

ul: The average worker's effective tax rate rises from 20.5 per cent in 2027–28 to 24.1 per cent in 2037–38, assuming real income growth of 1.2 per cent a year.
By 2034–35, tax rates rise by more than 2 percentage points for everyone earning more than $21,000 (in 2025 dollars), except the top 1 per cent.
The largest rise, more than 5 percentage points, is for people earning around $45,000.
For someone on about $45,000, 56 per cent of real income gains would go in extra tax. For someone near $190,000, around the top tax threshold, it would be 65 per cent.

body: "Bracket creep is neither an equitable nor a credible mechanism for restoring fiscal balance," the authors write.

body.h: Why it matters for the budget

body: The federal budget's projected return to surplus relies heavily on bracket creep, the note says. ABC News reported that the Parliamentary Budget Office estimates the budget would show a deficit of 0.7 per cent of GDP by the end of the decade without it, rather than the projected surplus of 1 per cent.
A decade with no tax cuts is unlikely in practice, the ABC noted, because governments have historically cut income tax every few years.

Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has promised to index tax brackets to inflation if the Coalition wins government, phased in from 2028, the ABC reported. Labor has said the plan would force unspecified and damaging spending cuts. Economist Saul Eslake told the ABC he supports indexation in principle but doubts spending cuts of the size needed are achievable.

body.note: This story explains published research. It is general information, not financial or tax advice.

body: Residents of Bupa aged care homes who want a cooked breakfast are being asked to sign up for a dining package costing about $42 a day, or $15,330 a year, the ABC has reported.

Residents who do not pay get a continental breakfast, according to the ABC. The package includes two hot breakfasts a week, an extra hot lunch choice each day, a lunch dessert, and a beer, wine or soft drink with lunch and dinner.
Bupa has more than 5,000 aged care residents across Australia, and the ABC reported that thousands could be affected.

Bupa told the ABC it would "provide additional cooked protein options for residents if recommended by a dietitian", whether or not they had chosen its enhanced dining option. In a statement, the company said: "We work hard to provide a consistently high standard of care and services to all our residents."

The charge falls under Higher Everyday Living Fees, or HELF, introduced as part of the federal government's aged care overhaul. HELF lets providers charge residents for optional extra services. The Weekly Source, an aged care industry publication, reported that Bupa's package is within the government's rules.

Aged Care Minister Sam Rae has said the government will change the rules so providers cannot charge a HELF for services that were already part of residents' care before 1 November 2025. The fee is meant for "optional, additional services people choose to receive", his statement says.

The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission told the ABC the law "does not prescribe particular foods, such as cooked eggs". It said it would review the information the ABC provided and assess whether further enquiries were needed.
Dietitians Australia president Fiona Willer told the ABC that many providers do not have dietitians on staff, and that it was not acceptable an egg at breakfast was "now seen as a luxury".

body.note: If you are unsure about a fee charged to a family member in aged care, ask the provider for the written agreement, and raise concerns with the provider or the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission. This is general information, not legal or financial advice.

en.dek: Residents who don't sign up get a continental breakfast. Bupa says dietitian-recommended cooked protein is available to everyone.
en.headline: Bupa aged care residents asked to pay about $42 a day for a package that includes hot breakfasts

body: Judges would have to treat an attack on someone who steps in to help another person as an aggravating factor when sentencing, under a law the Victorian Coalition says it will introduce if it wins the state election on 28 November.

Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has named the proposal Aidan's Law, after Aidan Becker, a 22-year-old off-duty security guard who died after he was stabbed at Mernda railway station, in Melbourne's north, in March while trying to help a 14-year-old boy. Ms Wilson said the policy followed a request from Mr Becker's mother, Natalie, AAP reported.
"If you're brave enough to stand up for someone else, the law should stand up for you," Ms Wilson said.

Victorian courts can already take that kind of circumstance into account, but the law does not specifically require them to, according to AAP. Details such as wording, penalties and timing were not part of the announcement as reported.

body.note: Several people have been charged in connection with Mr Becker's death. The case is before the courts.

body: Premier Ben Carroll promised 200 more police reservists, former officers who would answer phones and staff counters at police stations, on top of 400 already being recruited. He also announced two new police stations and the rebuilding or upgrading of four others, AAP reported.
"Victorians have been very clear that they want to see someone at the counter when they walk into their local station," Mr Carroll said.
The Labor government has started a review of Victoria's sentencing laws, with public consultation due to begin in April 2027.
Early voting opens on Wednesday 18 November, and election day is Saturday 28 November.
en.dek: Jess Wilson says courts would have to treat an attack on a Good Samaritan as more serious if the Coalition wins on 28 November. Labor is promising 200 more police reservists.

body: Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has confirmed the Coalition will put Labor, the Greens and the Socialists at the bottom of its how-to-vote cards for the 28 November state election, which means One Nation will be ranked above them where it is standing.

"We have made the decision that we will be putting Labor, the Greens, the Socialists at the bottom of the ticket," Ms Wilson said on Tuesday, according to the ABC. "The only way to change the government is a number one next to Liberal and Nationals."

She said the order would be decided case by case, electorate by electorate, after checking each candidate. The Coalition has not yet said which seats will see One Nation placed directly after its own candidate.
The confirmation follows a report in The Australian on Monday that the Nationals had already resolved to preference One Nation ahead of Labor and that the Liberals were expected to follow.

Labor minister Anthony Carbines said Labor's position was "very clear about putting One Nation at the bottom", and accused the Coalition and One Nation of "nudge-nudge wink-wink" arrangements, the ABC reported. Premier Ben Carroll called the announcement a reversal of Ms Wilson's earlier position, The Australia Today reported.

On Wednesday, federal Labor MP Julian Hill, the member for Bruce, called it a deal between the two parties: "If it looks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it's a duck." Federal Liberal MP Aaron Violi, the member for Casey, said he was "comfortable" with the decision. "The preference recommendations are not making judgement calls on every single comment, policy or portfolio," he said.
One Nation welcomed the decision, The Australia Today reported. On the same day, the party dropped its candidate for Preston over social media posts praising Adolf Hitler.

Labor is facing criticism of its own. It will not direct preferences in the Liberal-held seat of Prahran, where it has previously preferenced the Greens, the ABC reported. Greens leader Ellen Sandell called the decision "shocking". "This is Labor admitting that they have more in common with One Nation and the Liberals," she said.

Victoria uses full preferential voting in the lower house: you must number every box. Parties hand out how-to-vote cards suggesting an order, and many voters follow them, so where each party asks its supporters to put its rivals can decide close seats once first preferences are counted.

body.note: Your vote is yours. How-to-vote cards are only suggestions: you can number the boxes in any order you choose, as long as every box is numbered.

en.dek: The Opposition Leader says Labor, the Greens and the Socialists will go last on Coalition cards, decided seat by seat. Labor calls it a deal; the Greens are angry at Labor's own call in Prahran.
en.headline: Coalition will put Labor and the Greens below One Nation on how-to-vote cards, Jess Wilson confirms

body: Cricket Australia (CA) will not open a new investigation into the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering scandal, its chief executive Todd Greenberg said on Tuesday, after former Test opener Usman Khawaja wrote that the whole team knew about it.
Speaking on radio station SEN, Greenberg said there were "specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others", according to ABC News and Reuters.

"We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again," he said. He added that CA was comfortable with the outcome of the original investigation, which found that only captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and batter Cameron Bancroft knew of the plan.

In his autobiography, Sabr, Khawaja writes that discussion of tampering with the ball was not limited to a few players, and that sandpaper had been used before the Cape Town Test. He was not interviewed in the 2018 inquiry, the ABC reported. He also wrote that ball-tampering was common in the Sheffield Shield and named Victoria as the state best at it.
Responding to critics on social media on Tuesday, Khawaja said he had no commercial motive for the book, Reuters reported.

ul: Warner, one of the three players banned in 2018, said on Instagram on Monday that Khawaja's account was "100 per cent accurate" and described the original investigation as rushed and botched.
Bancroft declined to comment on Monday, Reuters reported. Former CA chief executive James Sutherland also declined to comment.
Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon denied knowledge of the plan in a joint statement in 2021.

body: Smith, Warner and Bancroft were banned or penalised by CA days after the incident in Cape Town in March 2018.

body.note: Earlier: Khawaja's book reopens Cape Town ball-tampering row, and Warner says his account is accurate.

en.dek: Chief executive Todd Greenberg says parts of Usman Khawaja's book contradict other accounts, and he sees no reason to revisit the 2018 Cape Town scandal.
en.headline: Cricket Australia won't reopen ball-tampering inquiry despite Khawaja's claims

body: David Jones will close 19 of its 38 stores, including three in Melbourne, after receivers took control of the 188-year-old department store chain.

Receivers FTI Consulting announced the closures on Wednesday. "The receivers have made the difficult decision to proceed with an urgent restructure of the business," they said, according to AAP. FTI said the steps were "unavoidable if David Jones is to continue as a viable business", The Nightly reported.
The Victorian stores closing are Glen Waverley, Highpoint (in Maribyrnong) and Malvern Central, according to SmartCompany and The Nightly.

The other closures are seven stores in New South Wales, three in Western Australia (including the Hay Street Mall store in central Perth), two each in Queensland and South Australia, one in the ACT and the chain's only New Zealand store, in Auckland.

The stores will keep trading for now and no final closure date has been set. "We anticipate they will cease trading by the end of the year," FTI said, according to The Nightly. Staff at affected stores are being consulted, and flagship stores in capital-city CBDs have largely been spared.
David Jones employs about 6,000 people. The receivers have not said how many jobs will go.

FTI was appointed receiver last week by lender Hilco Capital, after McGrathNicol was appointed voluntary administrator, SmartCompany reported. The business had reportedly not paid rent to Westfield owner Scentre Group since September. Expressions of interest from potential buyers are due by the end of this week.
Charles Lloyd Jones, a member of the founding family who left the business in 1993, told AAP: "If you don't have a unique offer, then it's a race to the bottom with price."

body.note: If you work at an affected store, the Fair Work Ombudsman (13 13 94) can explain your rights in a closure or insolvency. This is general information, not legal advice.

en.dek: Receivers say an urgent restructure is needed. Most closing stores are in the suburbs; city flagships largely survive.

body: More than $450,000 has been raised for the family of Feng Jianming, the food delivery rider killed near Queen Victoria Market on Friday night, as a Footscray man faced court charged with his murder.

Roberto Urbano, 51, of Footscray, has been charged with murder and intentionally causing serious injury. He appeared at Melbourne Magistrates' Court by video link on Monday and is due back in court on 26 April.

Mr Feng, 47, was a father of two from Shaanxi province in China who had lived in Australia for about nine years, the ABC reported. He was stabbed on Frederick Way at about 8pm on 6 November. A 34-year-old rider was seriously injured and taken to hospital.

body.note: This case is before the courts. The Melbourne Indian will not publish anything that could affect a fair trial.

body: The GoFundMe appeal was set up by the Melbourne Chinatown Business Association. Flowers have been left near the State Library.

Delivery platform HungryPanda said it was helping Mr Feng's family with visas, funeral arrangements, finances and insurance. The Transport Workers Union has questioned what the company does to manage risks for riders.

body: Lord Mayor Nick Reece said police would be "flooding the zone" in the central city until the end of the year, and that crime there had fallen 5.9 per cent over 12 months.
Assistant Commissioner Jo Stafford said Operation Harmony had doubled police resources in the CBD, but that police "can't solve this problem alone".

ul: In an emergency, call Triple Zero (000).
To report information to police, call Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000.
Most delivery apps have an in-app safety or emergency button; check where yours is before your next shift.
The Transport Workers Union represents delivery riders and can advise on safety and insurance.

body: Several long-running disability advocacy services have lost their federal funding as the government replaces a decades-old program with a new one, and a legal service in regional Victoria says it can no longer take on new clients.

Villamanta Disability Rights Legal Service is losing 30 per cent of its total funding, ABC News reported on Thursday. Its chief executive, Annie Nash, told the ABC the cut would mean job losses and less support for people with disability. She said it was hard to understand after a departmental review in March recognised Villamanta as a leader in the sector.

Cherry Baylosis, acting chief executive of Disability Advocacy Network Australia, told the ABC the changes were out of touch with what people with disability need, and warned that people could be left to handle crises alone or families and carers expected to fill the gap.

The Department told the ABC the new funding model responds to recommendations from the disability royal commission. It said up to $184 million, excluding GST, is available over six years from 2026-27 to 2031-32, through an open, competitive grant that both existing and new organisations could apply for.

Services funded under the old program will keep receiving money until February 2027 to help them transition. The changeover takes effect at the end of November. The Department did not say how many organisations had missed out.

The advocacy changes come as the government slows the growth of the National Disability Insurance Scheme. Cuts to therapy funding and to some support worker categories began on 1 October. The government expects about 240,000 participants to leave the scheme over four years, saving more than $38 billion, the ABC reported. The NDIS supports more than 782,000 people and costs more than $50 billion a year.

body.note: If you need help with an NDIS decision, you can ask for an internal review within three months of the decision. Independent advocates can help; the Disability Gateway (1800 643 787) can point you to one.

en.dek: Villamanta Disability Rights Legal Service is losing almost a third of its funding as Canberra replaces a decades-old advocacy program. The Department says the new model follows the disability royal commission.

body: Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November this year, the date set by the lunar calendar. For many Hindu, Sikh and Jain families in Melbourne, the day brings prayers, lamps, sweets and visits to family and friends.

Public celebrations started early. Melbourne Diwali, a free festival run by the not-for-profit SarasCare, was scheduled for Saturday 31 October at Marvel Stadium Square in Docklands, from 2pm to 10pm.

On Saturday 7 November the Immigration Museum on Flinders Street held a day of free Diwali activities, including henna, rangoli and traditional games. In ticketed Indian embroidery workshops, visitors added their own work to a shared 10-metre textile artwork.

Many Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras across Melbourne hold special prayers and services around Diwali. For Sikhs, the day is also Bandi Chhor Divas, which marks the release of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji from imprisonment. Check with your local temple or gurdwara for times.

The next major date for many in the community is the Gurpurab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji later this month. Published calendars list it on 24 or 25 November, depending on the calendar and time zone used, so confirm the dates of nagar kirtans and services with your gurdwara.
en.dek: Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November this year. Celebrations across the city began a week earlier.

body: चंद्र पंचांग के अनुसार इस साल दिवाली रविवार, 8 नवंबर को है। मेलबर्न में बहुत से हिंदू, सिख और जैन परिवारों के लिए यह दिन पूजा, दीयों, मिठाइयों और अपनों से मिलने-जुलने का दिन है।

सार्वजनिक उत्सव पहले ही शुरू हो गए थे। गैर-लाभकारी संस्था SarasCare द्वारा आयोजित निःशुल्क 'मेलबर्न दिवाली' उत्सव शनिवार, 31 अक्टूबर को डॉकलैंड्स के मार्वल स्टेडियम स्क्वेयर में दोपहर 2 बजे से रात 10 बजे तक होना तय था।

शनिवार, 7 नवंबर को फ़्लिंडर्स स्ट्रीट स्थित इमिग्रेशन म्यूज़ियम में दिवाली की निःशुल्क गतिविधियाँ हुईं, जिनमें मेहंदी, रंगोली और पारंपरिक खेल शामिल थे। टिकट वाली भारतीय कढ़ाई कार्यशालाओं में लोगों ने 10 मीटर लंबी साझा कपड़ा-कलाकृति में अपना योगदान जोड़ा।

दिवाली के आसपास मेलबर्न के कई हिंदू मंदिरों और सिख गुरुद्वारों में विशेष पूजा और दीवान होते हैं। सिखों के लिए यह दिन बंदी छोड़ दिवस भी है, जो गुरु हरगोबिंद साहिब जी की क़ैद से रिहाई की याद में मनाया जाता है। समय जानने के लिए अपने नज़दीकी मंदिर या गुरुद्वारे से संपर्क करें।

समुदाय में बहुतों के लिए अगली बड़ी तारीख़ इसी महीने गुरु नानक देव जी का प्रकाश पर्व (गुरपुरब) है। अलग-अलग कैलेंडर और समय-क्षेत्र के हिसाब से प्रकाशित पंचांगों में इसकी तारीख़ 24 या 25 नवंबर दी गई है, इसलिए नगर कीर्तन और दीवानों की तारीख़ अपने गुरुद्वारे से पक्की कर लें।

body: ਚੰਦਰ ਕੈਲੰਡਰ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਇਸ ਸਾਲ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਐਤਵਾਰ, 8 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਹੈ। ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੇ ਹਿੰਦੂ, ਸਿੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਜੈਨ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਇਹ ਦਿਨ ਅਰਦਾਸ-ਪੂਜਾ, ਦੀਵਿਆਂ, ਮਠਿਆਈਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਣ ਦਾ ਦਿਨ ਹੈ।

ਜਨਤਕ ਜਸ਼ਨ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋ ਗਏ ਸਨ। ਗੈਰ-ਮੁਨਾਫ਼ਾ ਸੰਸਥਾ SarasCare ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕਰਵਾਇਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ 'ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ' ਮੇਲਾ ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ, 31 ਅਕਤੂਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਡੌਕਲੈਂਡਜ਼ ਦੇ ਮਾਰਵਲ ਸਟੇਡੀਅਮ ਸਕੁਏਅਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੁਪਹਿਰ 2 ਵਜੇ ਤੋਂ ਰਾਤ 10 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਹੋਣਾ ਤੈਅ ਸੀ।

ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ, 7 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਫ਼ਲਿੰਡਰਜ਼ ਸਟ੍ਰੀਟ ਸਥਿਤ ਇਮੀਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਮਿਊਜ਼ੀਅਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ ਗਤੀਵਿਧੀਆਂ ਹੋਈਆਂ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਹਿੰਦੀ, ਰੰਗੋਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਵਾਇਤੀ ਖੇਡਾਂ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਸਨ। ਟਿਕਟ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਕਢਾਈ ਵਰਕਸ਼ਾਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੇ 10 ਮੀਟਰ ਲੰਮੀ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਕੱਪੜਾ-ਕਲਾਕ੍ਰਿਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਪਾਇਆ।

ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਆਸ-ਪਾਸ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਕਈ ਹਿੰਦੂ ਮੰਦਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਪੂਜਾ ਅਤੇ ਦੀਵਾਨ ਸਜਦੇ ਹਨ। ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਲਈ ਇਹ ਦਿਨ ਬੰਦੀ ਛੋੜ ਦਿਵਸ ਵੀ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਹਰਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਕੈਦ ਤੋਂ ਰਿਹਾਈ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਨਾਇਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੇਂ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੇ ਨੇੜਲੇ ਮੰਦਰ ਜਾਂ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਕਰੋ।

ਭਾਈਚਾਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਹੁਤਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਅਗਲੀ ਵੱਡੀ ਤਰੀਕ ਇਸੇ ਮਹੀਨੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਪੁਰਬ ਹੈ। ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਕੈਲੰਡਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਮਾਂ-ਖੇਤਰਾਂ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਛਪੀਆਂ ਜੰਤਰੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਸਦੀ ਤਰੀਕ 24 ਜਾਂ 25 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ, ਇਸ ਲਈ ਨਗਰ ਕੀਰਤਨ ਅਤੇ ਦੀਵਾਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਰੀਕ ਆਪਣੇ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਪੱਕੀ ਕਰ ਲਓ।

body: Early voting for the Victorian state election opens on Wednesday 18 November, and the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC) has now published where it will happen.

The VEC's venue list, correct as at 7 November, names 211 early voting centres across the state's 88 districts. They are open from 9am to 6pm every day from Wednesday 18 to Friday 27 November, except Sunday 22 November, when they are closed. You do not need a reason to vote early.
Below are the centres the VEC lists for the seven districts where at least one in 10 residents was born in India. Some centres serve more than one district.

body: The VEC's planning estimates suggest some of these centres will be among the busiest. It expects about 24,000 early votes at Connect City Church West in Hoppers Crossing, about 23,000 at the Salicki Avenue centre in Epping and about 22,000 at the 1st Cranbourne Scout Hall. If you can, avoid the last few days before election day.

The VEC rates every centre for wheelchair access. Several on this list, including Connect City Church West, the 1st Werribee and 1st Cranbourne scout halls and the Yellowbox Drive centre in Craigieburn, are rated as having limited or no wheelchair access. The VEC's venue locator shows the rating and entrance details for each centre.

If you will be overseas, the VEC has voting venues in 30 cities across 21 countries. Its list includes the Australian High Commission in New Delhi for in-person voting and postal vote drop-off. Check the VEC's overseas venue list for opening dates and hours before you go. You can also apply for a postal vote until 6pm on Wednesday 25 November.
Election day is Saturday 28 November, when voting centres are open from 8am to 6pm.
