body: Eleven Australian soldiers killed in the First World War, and commemorated for more than a century as unknown, have been formally identified, the federal government announced for Remembrance Day.

Five of the men were from Victoria: Sergeant Charles Henry Nicholls of Ballarat, Lieutenant Howard Victor Morey of Lilydale, Second Lieutenant James Albert McMichael of Melbourne, Corporal Harry Maitland Whiteoak of Preston and Lance Corporal Alexander Joseph Jack of Brunswick, according to the list reported by ABC News and NCA NewsWire.

The identifications drew on historical research, archaeological work and DNA analysis. The Army's Unrecovered War Casualties team, the Office of Australian War Graves and the Commonwealth War Graves Commission did the work, with help from French authorities, independent researchers and the soldiers' descendants.

Four of the men served with the 2nd Australian Field Ambulance, the unit that included Corporal Whiteoak and Lance Corporal Jack. NCA NewsWire reported that all four were killed on 5 May 1917, during the Second Battle of Bullecourt in France, when an artillery shell hit a regimental aid post set up in a railway cutting. The Army team recovered them during an excavation at Riencourt-lès-Cagnicourt in April 2025.

body: Lieutenant Anderson was killed near Ypres in Belgium on 20 September 1917, aged 23. ABC News reported that his comrades buried him by the roadside under a wooden cross, and that an unknown soldier recovered from almost the same spot in 1919, whose grave record noted "Anderson on shirt", was reburied at Hooge Crater Cemetery. His headstone there can now carry his name.

Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles, whose great-uncle was Lieutenant Anderson, said the identification was "deeply personal" for his family, ABC News reported. Veterans' Affairs Minister Matt Keogh said the work would "provide long-awaited answers for families" after generations of uncertainty.

body.note: Indian soldiers also fought beside the Anzacs at Gallipoli. Our Remembrance Day feature on them is in the Community section.

body: Federation University says it is not cutting 87 per cent of its arts subjects, after some staff were told in late October that the subjects would go, the ABC reported on Tuesday 10 November.

Staff at that meeting were also told the Bachelor of Criminal Justice would be cut at every campus except Berwick, according to the ABC. The university has called the meeting a "miscommunication", and the ABC understands it was not authorised by management.

In a statement reported by the ABC, a university spokesperson said Federation was "reviewing courses and units with low student numbers", but that humanities, social work and visual arts "remain important parts of Federation's teaching offering". The spokesperson pointed to the federal government's Job-ready Graduates policy, which raised student contributions for many humanities courses.

Staff across the university's campuses walked off the job for 24 hours on Monday 9 November after eight months of enterprise agreement negotiations failed to produce a deal, the ABC reported. More than 50 staff walked off at the Ballarat campus.

The National Tertiary Education Union says staff want a better pay offer, job security, fair workloads and a say in future decisions. Mathew Abbott, a senior lecturer in humanities and president of the union's Federation branch, told the ABC staff "were given just hours to make submissions" on the proposed cuts, and that the union had lodged a formal complaint.
The ABC reported that further work stoppages are planned for the week starting 16 November, which staff said could delay students receiving grades and results.

body.note: Federation University has campuses in Ballarat, Berwick, Gippsland, Melbourne and the Wimmera. If you are a student worried about your results or course, contact the university's student services directly.

en.dek: Some staff were told 87 per cent of arts subjects would go. The university now calls that a miscommunication, while its union pushes on with industrial action.

body: The Greens are aiming to take seats from Labor in Melbourne's inner north and west at the state election on Saturday 28 November, with Northcote shaping as their closest contest, the ABC reported on Tuesday.

The Greens currently hold two lower-house seats, Melbourne and Richmond. Brunswick, which they won in 2022, has been vacant since the death of Greens MP Tim Read, AAP reported. As well as Brunswick, the ABC says the party is targeting the Labor-held seats of Northcote, Preston, Pascoe Vale and Footscray, and the Liberal-held seat of Prahran.

Northcote was held by Lidia Thorpe, now a federal senator, after she won a 2017 by-election. At the 2022 election, Labor's Kat Theophanous held it against Greens candidate Campbell Gome by 184 votes, the ABC said. Both are standing again.

Mr Gome told the ABC's 7.30 program that voters kept telling him Labor had "abandoned communities like ours". Ms Theophanous said she expected another close result and rejected that claim, telling the program: "I don't think we've abandoned ordinary people."
The Victorian Socialists are also running in Northcote. Their candidate, Kath Larkin, told the ABC she did not expect to win but that the party's votes could be decisive in where preferences flow.

ul: The ABC reports Labor holds 54 of the 88 lower-house seats, the Coalition 29, and five sit on the crossbench.
The ABC says recent Redbridge and DemosAU polls put the Greens' statewide primary vote between 14 and 17 per cent, after Labor replaced Jacinta Allan with Ben Carroll as premier.
1,037 candidates are standing across the state, according to the Victorian Electoral Commission.

body: Several of the seats the Greens are targeting, including Footscray, Pascoe Vale and Preston, are home to sizeable migrant communities, so preference flows there could shape the result for many readers.

body.note: Voting is compulsory for enrolled Victorians aged 18 and over. Check who is standing in your district on the VEC website. Reporting in this story draws on the ABC's coverage.

en.dek: The Greens are targeting Northcote, Preston, Pascoe Vale and Footscray at the 28 November election. In Northcote, 184 votes decided the seat last time.

body: Borrowers with a variable home loan at any of the big four banks will pay more from Friday 13 November, when the banks lift their variable rates by 0.25 percentage points.

The rises follow the Reserve Bank's decision on 3 November to increase the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85 per cent. Commonwealth Bank, NAB, ANZ and Westpac each announced the following day that they would pass on the full increase, all from 13 November.

ANZ said the rise adds about $79 a month to principal-and-interest repayments on a $500,000 owner-occupier variable loan. The exact change for any household depends on the loan size, the rate and the time left on the loan. Banks usually write to customers with their new repayment amount.

dl: Variable home loan rates up 0.25 percentage points from 13 November. The bank's release did not mention savings rates.

Variable home loan rates up 0.25 percentage points from 13 November. The bonus rate on its ANZ Plus Growth Saver also rises 0.25 points, to a total of 5.60 per cent.
Variable home loan rates up 0.25 percentage points from 13 November, for new and existing customers. The Westpac Life total variable rate with bonus interest rises to 5.50 per cent.

body: All four banks urged customers who are struggling to get in touch early. "If things are getting tight, please don't wait until you're struggling to make a repayment," said NAB's Ana Marinkovic. CBA's Angus Sullivan said: "For customers who may be concerned about their financial position, we encourage them to contact us early."

In its November Statement on Monetary Policy, the Reserve Bank said headline inflation was 3.9 per cent in the year to the September quarter. It expects inflation "to remain above 3 per cent until late 2027, reflecting recent increases in fuel and other conflict-related costs and greater domestic capacity pressures". The Board said it "will continue to do what it considers necessary to bring inflation sustainably back to target".

body.h: If you are worried about repayments

ul: Call your lender before you miss a payment. Banks have hardship teams and must consider requests for help.
Check whether your rate is still competitive: a lender or a licensed mortgage broker can compare options.
The National Debt Helpline (1800 007 007) gives free, confidential financial counselling. Interpreters are available through TIS National on 131 450.

body.note: This story explains announced rate changes. It is general information, not financial advice. Check your own loan with your lender or a licensed adviser.

body: The value of new home loans across Australia fell 15.5 per cent in the September quarter, the largest quarterly fall since the Australian Bureau of Statistics series began in 2002, figures released on Wednesday show.
About 111,900 new home loans worth $81.2 billion were taken out in the three months to September, down 15 per cent in number on the June quarter.

Loans to investors fell 30.6 per cent in number and 32.3 per cent in value, the largest quarterly falls on record for both measures, the ABS said. It was the third quarter in a row of falls, and investor lending dropped in every state and territory.

"While lending activity fell across all borrower types in the September quarter, the decline was sharpest for investors," said Dr Mish Tan, the ABS head of finance statistics. "Our data suggests that investor activity is being influenced by factors beyond increasing borrowing costs."
J.P. Morgan economist Tom Ryan told the ABC that tax changes for investment properties announced in the federal budget had "likely exacerbated the decline".
Loans to owner-occupiers fell 5.3 per cent in number. In Victoria the fall was 6.6 per cent, compared with 10.4 per cent in Queensland and 4.1 per cent in New South Wales.
The number of loans to first home buyers fell 8.6 per cent in the quarter and was 12.3 per cent lower than a year earlier. First home buyers still made up more than a third of owner-occupier loans.
Housing Minister Clare O'Neil told Seven's Sunrise program, as reported by AAP: "What we're seeing is that more first home buyers are winning auctions that they're competing in."

Melbourne home values fell 0.8 per cent in October, the smallest fall of the five biggest cities, according to property data firm Cotality, AAP reported. Cotality's head of research, Gerard Burg, said affordability and investor policies were likely to remain constraints on the market.

body: When Prime Minister Anthony Albanese hosted Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the third Australia–India Annual Summit in Melbourne in July, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA). Modi said the two countries had decided to "work at a fast pace" on the CECA and on a bilateral investment treaty.

India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Australia's Trade Minister Don Farrell discussed speeding up the negotiations when they met on the sidelines of the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee on 30 September and 1 October, according to a post by Goyal. No timetable for concluding the agreement has been announced, The Indian Sun reported.

The interim Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) has been in force since 29 December 2022. From 1 January 2026, eligible Indian goods gained duty-free access across all Australian tariff lines, subject to rules of origin.
India was Australia's sixth-largest trading partner in 2025, with two-way trade in goods and services worth A$50.2 billion, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

ul: A Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation, and a new partnership on cyber, critical technologies and supply chains.
An arrangement enabling long-term Australian uranium exports to India, for peaceful purposes only and under international (IAEA) safeguards.
Approval for Melbourne's Victoria University to operate a campus in Gurugram, and a letter of intent for a Flinders University campus in Bengaluru.
$10 million for the Centre for Australia-India Relations' Maitri grants, which support business and people-to-people links.
A temporary space tracking terminal on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands to support India's Gaganyaan human spaceflight program.

body: "Our partnership has never been stronger," Albanese said after the talks. Modi said the relationship was "not just a partnership for the present; it is also a partnership for the future."

body: India has overtaken England as the most common overseas country of birth for people living in Australia, according to Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released on 29 April 2026.

About 971,000 India-born people were living in Australia at 30 June 2025, with the England-born population also at about 971,000. India narrowly overtook England during 2025, the first time it has held the top position.

The India-born population also recorded the largest increase of any birthplace group since 2015, rising by 522,000. The Italy-born and England-born populations recorded the largest decreases over the same period.
Overall, 8.8 million people living in Australia, or 32 per cent of the population, were born overseas.

The milestone was noted in July, when Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met in Melbourne. Their joint statement said the Indian community in Australia was "now Australia's largest overseas-born group".

body.note: The ABS release did not include a state-by-state breakdown. We will report Victorian figures when they are published.

body: ऑस्ट्रेलियन ब्यूरो ऑफ़ स्टैटिस्टिक्स (ABS) के 29 अप्रैल 2026 को जारी आँकड़ों के अनुसार, ऑस्ट्रेलिया में रहने वालों के विदेशी जन्म-देश के रूप में भारत ने इंग्लैंड को पीछे छोड़ दिया है।

30 जून 2025 तक ऑस्ट्रेलिया में भारत में जन्मे लगभग 9 लाख 71 हज़ार लोग रह रहे थे, और इंग्लैंड में जन्मे लोगों की संख्या भी लगभग इतनी ही थी। 2025 के दौरान भारत मामूली अंतर से इंग्लैंड से आगे निकला, और यह पहली बार है जब भारत शीर्ष पर पहुँचा है।

2015 के बाद से किसी भी जन्म-देश समूह में सबसे बड़ी बढ़ोतरी भी भारत में जन्मे लोगों की रही, जिनकी संख्या 5 लाख 22 हज़ार बढ़ी। इसी अवधि में इटली और इंग्लैंड में जन्मे लोगों की संख्या में सबसे ज़्यादा गिरावट आई।
कुल मिलाकर ऑस्ट्रेलिया में रहने वाले 88 लाख लोग, यानी आबादी का 32 प्रतिशत, विदेश में जन्मे हैं।

body: ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਅਨ ਬਿਊਰੋ ਆਫ਼ ਸਟੈਟਿਸਟਿਕਸ (ABS) ਵੱਲੋਂ 29 ਅਪ੍ਰੈਲ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਜਾਰੀ ਅੰਕੜਿਆਂ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਵਿਦੇਸ਼ੀ ਜਨਮ-ਦੇਸ਼ ਵਜੋਂ ਭਾਰਤ ਨੇ ਇੰਗਲੈਂਡ ਨੂੰ ਪਿੱਛੇ ਛੱਡ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ।

30 ਜੂਨ 2025 ਤੱਕ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੰਮੇ ਲਗਭਗ 9 ਲੱਖ 71 ਹਜ਼ਾਰ ਲੋਕ ਰਹਿ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ, ਅਤੇ ਇੰਗਲੈਂਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੰਮੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਵੀ ਲਗਭਗ ਏਨੀ ਹੀ ਸੀ। 2025 ਦੌਰਾਨ ਭਾਰਤ ਮਾਮੂਲੀ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਨਾਲ ਇੰਗਲੈਂਡ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਿਕਲਿਆ, ਅਤੇ ਇਹ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਵਾਰ ਹੈ ਜਦੋਂ ਭਾਰਤ ਸਿਖਰ 'ਤੇ ਪਹੁੰਚਿਆ ਹੈ।

2015 ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਨਮ-ਦੇਸ਼ ਸਮੂਹ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਵਾਧਾ ਵੀ ਭਾਰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੰਮੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦਾ ਰਿਹਾ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ 5 ਲੱਖ 22 ਹਜ਼ਾਰ ਵਧੀ। ਇਸੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਇਟਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਇੰਗਲੈਂਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੰਮੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਕਮੀ ਆਈ।
ਕੁੱਲ ਮਿਲਾ ਕੇ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ 88 ਲੱਖ ਲੋਕ, ਯਾਨੀ ਆਬਾਦੀ ਦਾ 32 ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ, ਵਿਦੇਸ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੰਮੇ ਹਨ।

body: ਜੁਲਾਈ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਦੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਐਂਥਨੀ ਅਲਬਨੀਜ਼ੀ ਅਤੇ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਨਰਿੰਦਰ ਮੋਦੀ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਿਲੇ, ਤਾਂ ਇਸ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਹੋਇਆ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਬਿਆਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਿਹਾ ਗਿਆ ਕਿ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਾ ਹੁਣ ਵਿਦੇਸ਼ੋਂ ਜੰਮੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਸਮੂਹ ਹੈ।

body.note: ABS ਦੀ ਇਸ ਰਿਲੀਜ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੂਬਾਵਾਰ ਅੰਕੜੇ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਨ। ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਦੇ ਅੰਕੜੇ ਛਪਣ 'ਤੇ ਅਸੀਂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਦੇਵਾਂਗੇ।

ਉੱਤਰੀ ਕੇਰਲ ਦੇ ਮਾਲਾਬਾਰ ਤਟ ਦੇ ਖਾਣੇ, ਸੰਗੀਤ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਚ ਦੀ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਾਮ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਖਾਣੇ ਦੇ ਸਟਾਲ, ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਪੇਸ਼ਕਾਰੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਕੱਪੜਿਆਂ ਤੇ ਗਹਿਣਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਸਟਾਲ ਹੋਣਗੇ। ਸੂਚੀ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਹਨਾਨ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਈਚੂ ਵੀ ਪੇਸ਼ਕਾਰੀ ਦੇਣਗੇ।

body: Indian passport, visa and other consular applications in Australia are now handled through six VFS Global centres, in Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, VFS Global said in July.

The Melbourne centre is on the ground floor of 324 St Kilda Road, Melbourne. Applicants book an appointment online through VFS Global's India–Australia portal. Applications are taken Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 4pm, except on public holidays and holidays declared by the Indian mission.
A VFS Global service charge of $115 per application applies from 23 July 2026, in addition to the Government of India fee, SBS Hindi reported, citing an announcement by the High Commission of India.

New passport and visa applications in Australia were suspended from 1 July while a dispute over the tender for India's outsourced consular services went through the Indian courts, Bloomberg reported. The High Commission of India in Canberra announced the restart on 23 July.

In May, SBS Hindi reported that India's Consul General in Melbourne, Anish Rajan, had announced a move from the Swanston Street office to a larger centre on St Kilda Road, with extra counters to shorten booking waits.

ul: Book only through the official VFS Global website for Indian services in Australia.
Check the current document checklist for your service before your appointment.
Allow extra time, as appointment availability can change, particularly around holidays.

body.note: Fees and procedures can change. Check the High Commission of India and VFS Global websites before you apply.

body: VFS ग्लोबल ने जुलाई में बताया कि ऑस्ट्रेलिया में भारतीय पासपोर्ट, वीज़ा और अन्य कांसुलर आवेदन अब छह VFS ग्लोबल केंद्रों से होते हैं: एडिलेड, ब्रिस्बेन, कैनबरा, मेलबर्न, पर्थ और सिडनी।

मेलबर्न केंद्र ग्राउंड फ़्लोर, 324 सेंट किल्डा रोड, मेलबर्न में है। आवेदकों को VFS ग्लोबल के भारत–ऑस्ट्रेलिया पोर्टल पर ऑनलाइन अपॉइंटमेंट बुक करनी होती है। आवेदन सोमवार से शुक्रवार, सुबह 8:30 से शाम 4 बजे तक जमा होते हैं, सार्वजनिक छुट्टियों और भारतीय मिशन द्वारा घोषित छुट्टियों को छोड़कर।
SBS हिंदी ने भारतीय उच्चायोग की घोषणा के हवाले से बताया कि 23 जुलाई 2026 से भारत सरकार के शुल्क के अलावा हर आवेदन पर $115 का VFS ग्लोबल सेवा शुल्क लगता है।

ब्लूमबर्ग के अनुसार, भारत की आउटसोर्स की गई कांसुलर सेवाओं के टेंडर को लेकर भारतीय अदालतों में चले विवाद के कारण 1 जुलाई से ऑस्ट्रेलिया में नए पासपोर्ट और वीज़ा आवेदन रोक दिए गए थे। कैनबरा स्थित भारतीय उच्चायोग ने 23 जुलाई को सेवाएँ फिर शुरू होने की घोषणा की।

मई में SBS हिंदी ने ख़बर दी थी कि मेलबर्न में भारत के महावाणिज्य दूत अनीश राजन ने स्वानस्टन स्ट्रीट कार्यालय की जगह सेंट किल्डा रोड पर एक बड़े केंद्र में जाने की घोषणा की है, जिसमें ज़्यादा काउंटर होंगे ताकि बुकिंग का इंतज़ार कम हो।

ul: अपॉइंटमेंट केवल ऑस्ट्रेलिया में भारतीय सेवाओं की आधिकारिक VFS ग्लोबल वेबसाइट से ही बुक करें।
अपॉइंटमेंट से पहले अपनी सेवा के लिए दस्तावेज़ों की ताज़ा सूची जाँच लें।
अतिरिक्त समय रखें, क्योंकि ख़ासकर छुट्टियों के आसपास अपॉइंटमेंट की उपलब्धता बदल सकती है।

body.note: शुल्क और प्रक्रियाएँ बदल सकती हैं। आवेदन से पहले भारतीय उच्चायोग और VFS ग्लोबल की वेबसाइट देख लें।

body: VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਨੇ ਜੁਲਾਈ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਪਾਸਪੋਰਟ, ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਹੁਣ ਛੇ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਕੇਂਦਰਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ: ਐਡੀਲੇਡ, ਬ੍ਰਿਸਬੇਨ, ਕੈਨਬਰਾ, ਮੈਲਬਰਨ, ਪਰਥ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਡਨੀ।

ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਗਰਾਊਂਡ ਫ਼ਲੋਰ, 324 ਸੇਂਟ ਕਿਲਡਾ ਰੋਡ, ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੈ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਕਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਦੇ ਭਾਰਤ–ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਪੋਰਟਲ 'ਤੇ ਆਨਲਾਈਨ ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟ ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰਨੀ ਪੈਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਸੋਮਵਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁੱਕਰਵਾਰ, ਸਵੇਰੇ 8:30 ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ਾਮ 4 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਹੁੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਛੁੱਟੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਐਲਾਨੀਆਂ ਛੁੱਟੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ।
SBS ਹਿੰਦੀ ਨੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਐਲਾਨ ਦੇ ਹਵਾਲੇ ਨਾਲ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ 23 ਜੁਲਾਈ 2026 ਤੋਂ ਭਾਰਤ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੀ ਫ਼ੀਸ ਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਹਰ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ 'ਤੇ $115 ਦੀ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਸੇਵਾ ਫ਼ੀਸ ਲੱਗਦੀ ਹੈ।

ਬਲੂਮਬਰਗ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, ਭਾਰਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਆਊਟਸੋਰਸ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਟੈਂਡਰ ਬਾਰੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਅਦਾਲਤਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਚੱਲੇ ਵਿਵਾਦ ਕਾਰਨ 1 ਜੁਲਾਈ ਤੋਂ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਵੀਆਂ ਪਾਸਪੋਰਟ ਅਤੇ ਵੀਜ਼ਾ ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ ਰੋਕ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ ਸਨ। ਕੈਨਬਰਾ ਸਥਿਤ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਨੇ 23 ਜੁਲਾਈ ਨੂੰ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਮੁੜ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ।

ਮਈ ਵਿੱਚ SBS ਹਿੰਦੀ ਨੇ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਸੀ ਕਿ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਕੌਂਸਲ ਜਨਰਲ ਅਨੀਸ਼ ਰਾਜਨ ਨੇ ਸਵਾਨਸਟਨ ਸਟ੍ਰੀਟ ਦਫ਼ਤਰ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਸੇਂਟ ਕਿਲਡਾ ਰੋਡ 'ਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਡੇ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਾਣ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਧ ਕਾਊਂਟਰ ਹੋਣਗੇ ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਬੁਕਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਉਡੀਕ ਘਟੇ।

ul: ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਆਸਟ੍ਰੇਲੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਤ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰੋ।
ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਆਪਣੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਲਈ ਦਸਤਾਵੇਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਾਜ਼ਾ ਸੂਚੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਲਓ।
ਵਾਧੂ ਸਮਾਂ ਰੱਖੋ, ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਕਰਕੇ ਛੁੱਟੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਆਸ-ਪਾਸ ਅਪੌਇੰਟਮੈਂਟਾਂ ਦੀ ਉਪਲਬਧਤਾ ਬਦਲ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

body.note: ਫ਼ੀਸਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆਵਾਂ ਬਦਲ ਸਕਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਹਾਈ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਅਤੇ VFS ਗਲੋਬਲ ਦੀਆਂ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟਾਂ ਦੇਖ ਲਓ।

body: The federal government has set the 2027 National Planning Level for new international student commencements at 295,000, unchanged from 2026, Study Australia announced in July.

The government says the planning level is not a cap on student numbers. Student visa applications are processed as a priority until a student's chosen provider reaches 80 per cent of its allocation. Applications after that point are still accepted but processed more slowly.
No active provider will receive a lower allocation in 2027 than in 2026, and TAFE students remain exempt from the planning level, The PIE News reported.

The student visa (subclass 500) application fee starts at A$2,500, according to the Department of Home Affairs. A lower fee applies to some applicants, including those enrolling in standalone English language (ELICOS) or non-award courses.
Education Minister Jason Clare said, as reported by The PIE News: "International education is an incredibly important export industry for Australia, but we need to manage it sustainably."

Melbourne's Victoria University received approval in July to open a campus in Gurugram, near Delhi. The university said the campus would teach through its block model, with students studying one subject at a time in four-week blocks, and that it was scheduled to open in August 2026.

body.note: This is general information, not migration advice. For advice about your circumstances, speak to a registered migration agent or check the Department of Home Affairs website.

en.dek: The federal government has kept the planning level for new international students at 295,000 for 2027, unchanged from this year.

body: Former Test opener Usman Khawaja has reopened one of Australian cricket's most painful episodes, writing in his new book, Sabr, that players and staff on the 2018 tour of South Africa knew about the ball-tampering plan that led to bans for three players.

David Warner, one of the three, backed Khawaja in a video on Instagram on Monday, calling his account "100 per cent accurate", the ABC reported. Warner also criticised Cricket Australia's 2018 investigation, saying Khawaja had not been interviewed and the process had been rushed.

Cricket Australia has consistently denied that all players and staff knew about the plan, according to the ABC. It is not yet known whether it will take any further action. Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, the other two players banned in 2018, had not commented publicly at the time of writing.

Khawaja also writes about the Sheffield Shield. As reported by the ABC, he says Victorian teams of the 2000s and 2010s were probably the best at altering the ball, because the MCG pitch was flat and reverse swing and spin were the way to win there. He writes that he never tampered with a ball himself but knew what was going on and regarded himself as complicit.
Victoria and Australia fast bowler Scott Boland, speaking in Melbourne on Monday, said he had not seen anything untoward and that reverse swing had largely gone out of the game since 2018.
The row lands weeks before Australia's home Tests against New Zealand, and ahead of the tour of India from January. Khawaja's book is released on Tuesday 10 November.

body.note: The claims in this story are Usman Khawaja's, from his book as reported by the ABC. They have not been tested, and others named in the wider debate dispute them.

en.dek: Usman Khawaja writes that the whole touring party knew about the 2018 plan and that Victoria were the Shield's best at the 'dark arts'. Scott Boland says he has seen nothing untoward.
en.headline: Khawaja's book reopens Cape Town ball-tampering row, and Warner says his account is accurate

body: Victorian Labor has promised $420 million to run more than 550 extra V/Line trips a week if it wins the state election on 28 November, with the largest increases on the lines through Melbourne's fast-growing west.
Premier Ben Carroll announced the plan on Thursday. Labor says it would grow regional train services by about a quarter, according to reports by the ABC and AAP.

body.h: What would change, line by line

ul: Wyndham Vale: 249 extra trips a week from 2027, on a dedicated service meant to ease crowding. Trains to Wyndham Vale also stop at Tarneit.
Melton: 162 extra trips a week from 2027, so trains run every 20 minutes. Longer nine-car trains, announced earlier, are also due next year.
Bendigo line: 101 extra trips a week from 2028, including 80 new services to Kyneton and 21 more to Bendigo.
Seymour line (through Donnybrook and Wallan): 29 extra trips a week from 2028, with trains every 40 minutes between peaks instead of hourly.
Geelong: more express services that cut about 10 minutes from the trip, and two extra Sunday services to Geelong and Waurn Ponds.
Ballarat: most weekday off-peak trains to run express to Melbourne from next year.
Warrnambool: eight extra weekend services from next year. Traralgon: one extra Sunday service from 2028.

body: AAP reported that new hybrid electric trains on the Melton and Wyndham Vale lines would free up 25 three-car V/Line trains for use elsewhere. Mr Carroll told AAP the new services would let Victorians "realise the benefits of Labor's upgrades".

The ABC said the pledge targets regional and outer-suburban seats where Labor is under pressure from the Coalition and One Nation. AAP reported that a poll by RedBridge and Accent Research for the Australian Financial Review, published on Wednesday, put the Coalition's primary vote at 31 per cent, Labor at 23, One Nation at 22 and the Greens at 15.

In September the Coalition promised to back more train capacity across the state, and it has pledged $1.7 billion for hybrid trains to Melton and Wyndham Vale, the ABC reported. The government has questioned whether that plan could work alongside the rest of the network.

body.h: A fight over the Liberals' surplus plan

body: Labor also released analysis it had asked the Parliamentary Budget Office to do on Liberal leader Jess Wilson's promise of a cash surplus by 2032, the ABC reported. Ms Wilson's plan relies mostly on shrinking the public service through attrition, which she says would save $22 billion over a decade.

According to the ABC, the budget office estimated the policy would save $8.5 billion by 2032, with most of the savings arriving later. Treasurer Colin Brooks said this showed a Wilson government would have to cut services such as health.

Ms Wilson said in a statement she would not take lectures on costings from Labor. "Only our Liberal and Nationals team has a costed and credible plan to repair the budget," she said, pointing to more than $26 billion in savings. The ABC noted that budget office results depend on the assumptions they are given, and that Ms Wilson has not released her own version of the analysis.

body.note: Election pledges are promises, not funded projects. We report what each party says it will do and link to our sources so you can check.

en.dek: Premier Ben Carroll says more than 550 extra regional trips a week would be added if Labor is re-elected on 28 November. Labor also used a budget office analysis to attack the Liberals' surplus plan.
en.headline: Labor promises $420 million for more V/Line trains, with Melton and Wyndham Vale getting the biggest boost

body: Students anywhere in Victoria would be able to study Hindi, Punjabi, Bengali or Tamil for VCE, even if their school does not teach it, under a $43 million election promise from Victorian Labor.

Premier Ben Carroll said a re-elected Labor government would expand online classes at the Victorian School of Languages (VSL) from the 17 VCE languages it teaches online now to all 44 modern VCE languages, starting in 2028. Labor also says it will explore adding Sanskrit.

"Learning a language doesn't just help young people stay connected to their past – it can unlock their future," Mr Carroll said. "Every Victorian student should have the opportunity to study the language they want, no matter where they live."
More than 16,000 Victorian students are studying a VCE language this year, and about 800 of them do it through VSL's online classes, according to the announcement.

For families in growth suburbs such as Tarneit, Truganina, Craigieburn and Cranbourne, the practical change is simple: a student whose school offers only French or Japanese could take Hindi or Punjabi online and have it count towards their VCE.

dl: Online VCE classes at the Victorian School of Languages, from 17 languages to all 44

body: Education Minister Gabrielle Williams said the investment would "give more students better access to language education". Mr Carroll added: "Labor will always back our Indian community."

In March, while he was Deputy Premier and Education Minister, Mr Carroll announced $150,000 in scholarships to train 18 Hindi and Punjabi teachers through Monash University, and $3.5 million for three schools to lead the teaching of the two languages: Alkira Secondary College in Cranbourne North and Wyndham Central College in Werribee for Hindi, and Mount Ridley P-12 College in Craigieburn for Punjabi.

Labor contrasted the promise with what it called a "$40 billion cuts agenda" from a "Liberal–One Nation Coalition". The Coalition, led by Jess Wilson, had not responded publicly to the languages pledge when it was announced on 8 November.

body.note: Election day is Saturday 28 November. Early voting opens on Wednesday 18 November.

en.dek: A re-elected Labor government would expand the Victorian School of Languages' online classes from 17 VCE languages to all 44 from 2028, and says it will explore adding Sanskrit.

body: Victorian Labor says it will introduce Clare's Law, a scheme that lets people ask police whether a partner has a history of family violence, if it is re-elected on 28 November.

Premier Ben Carroll and Attorney-General Sonya Kilkenny announced the pledge on Tuesday in Fraser Rise, in Melbourne's north-west, the ABC reported. "You deserve to know if your partner has a secret violent past," Mr Carroll said.

ul: A family violence disclosure scheme modelled on South Australia's, which has run since 2018. People could also ask about the partner of a family member or friend they think is at risk, and AAP reports police could share information with people they believe are in danger.
A new criminal offence for people convicted of family violence or sexual offences to use dating apps.

A wider ban on smart glasses, extending to swimming pools, change rooms, community sports venues, hospitals, aged care and family violence services. Smart glasses are already being banned in schools, kindergartens and childcare.
$15.5 million more for The Orange Door, which Labor says would help an extra 10,000 victim-survivors, and $16 million for a new Early Intervention and Prevention Fund.
Power for coroners to appoint an alternative next of kin in cases involving family violence allegations, charges or estrangement.

body: The opposition promised in July to introduce a domestic violence disclosure scheme within 100 days if it wins government, according to the ABC and AAP. AAP reported that Labor voted down a similar Coalition private member's bill in November 2024.
Asked why Labor had not acted sooner, Ms Kilkenny said the government had consulted the family violence sector, and criticised "promises made by the opposition without consulting with the sector".
No start date for the scheme was given.

body.note: If you or someone you know is affected by family violence, call 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or Safe Steps on 1800 015 188, any time. In an emergency, call 000.

en.dek: Victorians could ask police whether a partner has a history of family violence under a scheme both major parties now say they will bring in.

body: Marnus Labuschagne will not be considered for Australia's four-Test series against New Zealand this summer, chair of selectors George Bailey said on Monday.

"This gives him a little bit of space and clears up a bit of conjecture," Bailey said. Asked whether Labuschagne could return for the tours of India and England, he said: "Still possible, absolutely."
The squad for the first Test, which starts in Perth on 9 December, will be named after round four of the Sheffield Shield. Labuschagne will captain Queensland in the Shield.

body: The Victorian Liberal Party has withdrawn its endorsement of Paul Lindemann, its candidate for the Labor-held seat of Williamstown in Melbourne's west, over comments about Indigenous Australians that came to light on Wednesday.

In a statement, the party said the views Mr Lindemann had expressed were "offensive, unacceptable and inconsistent with the values and standards expected of Liberal candidates", the ABC reported. It said all candidates were expected to treat Australians with dignity and respect, that Mr Lindemann's comments "fell short of that standard", and that it had not previously been aware of them.

The Age reported that the comments were posted from an anonymous Facebook account, named after Mr Lindemann's yacht, that it linked to him. It reported that in posts about the proposed Voice to Parliament, the account described Indigenous Australians as "never civilised".
Earlier on Wednesday, Sport Minister Steve Dimopoulos called on Opposition Leader Jess Wilson to drop Mr Lindemann over his conduct as a junior basketball coach, the ABC reported.

Mr Lindemann was suspended for six weeks last year for bringing the game into disrepute after an under-14 girls' game, The Age and 7NEWS reported. He told The Age he had acted on his "first instinct" to protect a player. In a statement, he apologised and said he should have "handled the situation differently", according to the ABC.
Nominations for the 28 November election have closed, so Mr Lindemann's name will stay on the Williamstown ballot paper, The Age reported.

Labor has held Williamstown for all but four years since 1889. Jobs Minister Melissa Horne has held the seat since 2018, and kept it at the last election with a two-party-preferred margin of 13.4 per cent, The Age reported.
The decision came a day after One Nation dropped its Preston candidate, Franco Guardiani, over social media posts praising Adolf Hitler.

body.note: A full list of candidates for every district is on the VEC website. If you see hateful content aimed at a community, Victoria's anti-vilification laws explain how to report it.

en.dek: The party says it was not aware of the comments before. Nominations have closed, so he will still appear on ballot papers in the Labor-held seat.
en.headline: Liberals drop Williamstown candidate Paul Lindemann over comments about Indigenous Australians, but his name stays on the ballot

body: The City of Melbourne's 2026–27 budget includes more than $1.2 million to keep developing a Little India precinct in Docklands. The council's aim is a recognisable cultural destination alongside Chinatown and Koreatown, built through infrastructure, events and creative projects.

The funding was first flagged in the council's draft budget in March. Councillor Philip Le Liu said at the time, Melbourning reported: "As Australia's most multicultural city, we're taking big steps to make Little India a reality."

In its response to budget consultation, the council said it would focus on "testing future ideas for Little India". It has committed to engaging extensively with Docklands residents and Indian communities, and to running trial experiences so people can try ideas and help shape future plans.
More than 550 people contributed to the council's wider budget consultation, which ran from 31 March to 28 April.
No opening date has been announced. Lord Mayor Nick Reece discussed the project with SBS Hindi in May, and SBS reported that he had invited Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an official opening.

Local newspaper Docklands News reported that the council's consultation summary found a minority of submissions supported a Little India in Docklands, while most urged caution about a single-theme precinct. Concerns included top-down delivery and money being diverted from the suburb's other needs, with many residents pointing to greening, shade, wind protection and better public spaces.

The council has kept the $1.2 million commitment but is taking a staged approach that starts with trial activations, the paper reported. Council officers have said no exact location has been chosen, and the council has committed to finalising a Docklands public realm improvements plan.

At a budget hearing on 12 May, Federation of Indian Associations of Victoria president Vasan Srinivasan called the funding a "positive and historic beginning", but said a world-class precinct would need between $5 million and $10 million, Docklands News reported.

The proposal has also drawn what The Australia Today described in April as "negative and, at times, racist commentary". Mr Srinivasan launched a petition in support of the precinct, the outlet reported.
Victoria's strengthened anti-vilification laws, which added new civil protections from 15 April 2026, apply to public conduct online as well as offline.

body.note: We will report consultation dates for Little India as soon as the council announces them.

en.dek: The City of Melbourne has set aside more than $1.2 million to develop a Little India precinct in Docklands, but no site has been chosen and many local residents have urged caution.

body: Macquarie Bank has admitted it failed to make sure the advertising for its savings account "Welcome Rate" was clear, and faces a proposed $14 million penalty, the corporate regulator ASIC said on Wednesday.
ASIC and Macquarie have jointly proposed the penalty to the NSW Supreme Court, which must still approve it.

Between December 2021 and September 2022, Macquarie advertised a four-month Welcome Rate for new savings customers, describing it as a "bonus". ASIC alleged customers could have thought it was paid on top of the standard variable rate. In fact, it generally replaced the standard rate.
As interest rates rose in 2022, the gap between the two rates shrank or disappeared. Where the standard rate rose above the Welcome Rate, customers simply received the standard rate.
Macquarie admitted breaching the Corporations Act. It had already paid $8.8 million to nearly 40,000 customers, ASIC said.
"Banks must get the basics right," ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland said.

In its statement, Macquarie said some of the wording on its website "was not sufficiently clear". "We apologise for any confusion caused," said Ben Perham, its head of banking and financial services. Macquarie said ASIC had acknowledged the conduct was not deliberate, and that it is reviewing its product descriptions.

In a separate warning, ASIC said Australians may be missing out on interest they were promised, because welcome, introductory and bonus rates often come with conditions or time limits. An ACCC inquiry found that in the first half of 2023, on average 71 per cent of bonus interest accounts did not get the bonus rate each month.
"If you have met the conditions for a higher rate but aren't receiving it, raise it with your bank," Mr Kirkland said.
ASIC suggests checking:

ul: the interest rate you are actually being paid
whether an advertised rate is introductory, promotional or conditional
what you must do each month to get the higher rate, such as deposits, no withdrawals or a minimum balance
how long a promotional rate lasts, and the rate that applies after it ends
whether another account offers a better rate or simpler conditions

body.note: ASIC's Moneysmart website has a guide to savings accounts. If your bank does not fix a problem, you can complain to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). This is general information, not financial advice.

en.dek: Nearly 40,000 customers have already been paid $8.8 million. The regulator says anyone on a bonus or introductory rate should check they are getting what they were promised.
en.headline: Macquarie Bank faces $14 million penalty over its savings 'Welcome Rate', as ASIC tells savers to check their interest

body: Staff at the Malmsbury Youth Justice Centre in central Victoria were paid almost $7 million in compensation over violent incidents at work, according to Department of Justice data released to the ABC under freedom of information laws.

The data covers January 2020 to December 2023, when the centre closed after riots and escapes. Over that period, an occupational violence incident was logged every 2.6 days on average, the ABC reported.

One former worker, Justin White, told the ABC he was attacked by detainees armed with a plastic cricket bat in October 2019, a few weeks into the job, and has not been able to work since. "I genuinely thought I wasn't going to come out of it," he said.

The government reopened Malmsbury in April 2026, first with 30 beds and later adding 45. Youth Justice Minister Ros Spence told Nationals MP Gaelle Broad in parliament that, as of 9 September, 22 young people were held there and more than 150 staff were employed.

Ms Spence said operations were being scaled up in stages so the department could recruit and train staff and "stress test operating processes". The department's annual report puts the capital works budget for the reopening at $17.6 million, the ABC reported.
As of 2 November, Victoria's youth justice facilities were at 63.5 per cent of combined capacity, with about 224 young people detained across three sites, the ABC reported.

Youth justice and crime are issues in the campaign for the 28 November state election. Labor has pledged to introduce rehabilitation detention for low and mid-level youth offenders, including at Malmsbury. The Coalition has promised 1,500 more police on top of Labor's recruitment target, and the Greens have called for more spending on mental health, drug and alcohol treatment and youth programs, as we reported in our story on Victoria's prisons.

body: A major Microsoft outage has left people around the world unable to use Outlook email, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services since early on Friday morning, Melbourne time.

Problems began at about 4.30am AEDT (12.30pm on Thursday in New York), TechRadar reported. Reports of Outlook problems on the tracking site Downdetector climbed past 120,000 as people found they could not open their inboxes, or send or receive email.

Microsoft's service health page said users might be unable to connect to Exchange Online (Outlook email), Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Copilot for Microsoft 365 and the Defender XDR security service, ABC News reported. Some other companies' tools that connect to Microsoft 365 were also hit.

Microsoft said the problem was not a surge in traffic but "a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable", which put extra load on the rest of its systems, according to the ABC. It paused all updates, moved traffic away from the affected infrastructure and restarted servers. It said it had not found any recent change linked to the start of the problem.

At about 8am AEDT, the Microsoft 365 Status account on X said Microsoft had "validated an alternative service health check method, which allowed a subset of affected servers to successfully return to service", and was applying the fix more widely. TechRadar reported shortly after that the situation was improving.
Microsoft has not said what caused the outage. IT administrators can follow incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin centre.

ul: You don't need to change your password or email settings: the problem is on Microsoft's side.
Emails sent during the outage may arrive late once services recover.
Be wary of emails or texts about the outage asking you to log in or click a link. Scammers often use big outages as cover.
Check Microsoft's service status page or your workplace IT team for updates.

body.note: This is a developing story. Last updated 8.45am AEDT, Friday 13 November.

en.dek: Email, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services went down early on Friday, Melbourne time. Microsoft says a fix is bringing servers back, but has not said what caused it.
en.headline: Microsoft outage knocks out Outlook and Teams worldwide; services starting to recover

body: Police divers are searching rivers in Gippsland as the hunt for a missing 17-year-old enters its fifth day.

William, who also goes by Will, was last seen at about 4pm on Friday 6 November near Stoney Creek Road, close to Walhalla East, Victoria Police said. He was camping with another teenager and walked a short distance to another part of the camp to collect equipment. When he did not return, the other teen searched but found no sign of him.
He was wearing a pair of shorts and work boots, police said. ABC News reported he left his phone, food and water behind.

The search is being run from a command post at Cowwarr and has widened to a larger area of dense bush, with a police helicopter, off-road motorbikes, Search and Rescue officers and SES crews, ABC News reported. About 40 to 50 people are searching on foot.
"There's nothing that we're not doing to try to find William, and we're still very hopeful that today might be the day," Acting Inspector Jason Benbow told the ABC.

ul: If you see William, call Triple Zero (000).
If you have information, call Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or Sale police station on (03) 5142 2200.

en.dek: William, who goes by Will, was last seen on Friday afternoon while camping near Walhalla East. Police say they are still hopeful.

body: A 27-year-old woman has been charged with trafficking heroin and methylamphetamine after detectives searched a unit in Mordialloc, in Melbourne's south-east, Victoria Police says.

Detectives from the Moorabbin Crime Investigation Unit executed a search warrant at the Crown Avenue unit at about 6.45am on Tuesday 10 November. Police say they found traffickable quantities of heroin and methylamphetamine, a hatchet, and items consistent with selling drugs. The release did not give the amounts.
Two women, aged 27 and 36, were arrested at the scene.

ul: Trafficking heroin and methylamphetamine
Possessing a controlled weapon
Dealing with property suspected of being proceeds of crime
Contravening bail

body: The 27-year-old appeared at Moorabbin Magistrates' Court on Tuesday and was remanded in custody to reappear on 4 December, police said. The 36-year-old was released and police intend to charge her on summons. Police did not name either woman.
Police say enquiries are continuing.

body.note: Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or at crimestoppersvic.com.au. You can stay anonymous. Charges are allegations that have not been tested in court.

en.dek: Detectives say they found traffickable quantities of both drugs, a hatchet and drug paraphernalia at a unit on Crown Avenue on Tuesday morning.

body: Community associations, temples, gurdwaras, cultural groups and trader associations can apply for Victorian Government funding, but most rounds open once a year and close within a few weeks. All three of the main 2026 programs below have now closed.

Grants ranged from $5,000 for smaller community events to $50,000 for events of any size, with a further $1 million set aside for events in rural and regional Victoria. Events had to be free, inclusive, accessible and culturally safe. Applications closed on 17 April 2026.

This $5 million program had three streams offering up to $10,000, $100,000 or $400,000 for skills, partnerships and leadership, and for day-to-day costs such as IT systems and business planning. Organisations from new and emerging communities, and from rural and regional areas, were a priority. Applications closed on 19 February 2026.

This fund offered $5,000 grants to not-for-profit business associations, such as trader groups and chambers of commerce, to run advice, training or mentoring for multicultural small business owners and their staff. Each project needed at least 10 participants. Applications closed at 4pm on 28 September 2026, and funded projects must be finished by 26 February 2027.

body.h: Getting ready for the next round

ul: Make sure your organisation has a current ABN and is registered with the right regulator. The business skills fund required both.
Keep a short description of your organisation, its members and its past events ready to adapt.
Watch the Victorian Government's multicultural grants pages from early in the year. In 2026 the capacity building and festivals rounds were announced in January and March.

body.note: Programs for 2027 have not been announced. Rules and amounts may change.

body: सामुदायिक संघ, मंदिर, गुरुद्वारे, सांस्कृतिक समूह और व्यापारी संघ विक्टोरियाई सरकार से फ़ंडिंग के लिए आवेदन कर सकते हैं, लेकिन ज़्यादातर दौर साल में एक बार खुलते हैं और कुछ ही हफ़्तों में बंद हो जाते हैं। नीचे दिए गए 2026 के तीनों मुख्य कार्यक्रम अब बंद हो चुके हैं।

छोटे सामुदायिक कार्यक्रमों के लिए $5,000 से लेकर किसी भी आकार के कार्यक्रम के लिए $50,000 तक के अनुदान थे, और ग्रामीण व क्षेत्रीय विक्टोरिया के कार्यक्रमों के लिए अलग से $1 मिलियन रखे गए। कार्यक्रमों का निःशुल्क, सबके लिए खुला, सुलभ और सांस्कृतिक रूप से सुरक्षित होना ज़रूरी था। आवेदन 17 अप्रैल 2026 को बंद हुए।

$5 मिलियन के इस कार्यक्रम में तीन श्रेणियाँ थीं, जिनमें कौशल, साझेदारी और नेतृत्व के लिए, और आईटी सिस्टम व व्यावसायिक योजना जैसे रोज़मर्रा के ख़र्चों के लिए $10,000, $100,000 या $400,000 तक मिल सकते थे। नए और उभरते समुदायों तथा ग्रामीण व क्षेत्रीय इलाक़ों के संगठनों को प्राथमिकता दी गई। आवेदन 19 फ़रवरी 2026 को बंद हुए।

इस कोष में गैर-लाभकारी व्यापार संघों, जैसे ट्रेडर समूहों और चैंबर ऑफ़ कॉमर्स, को $5,000 के अनुदान दिए गए, ताकि वे बहुसांस्कृतिक छोटे व्यवसायों के मालिकों और कर्मचारियों के लिए सलाह, प्रशिक्षण या मार्गदर्शन दे सकें। हर परियोजना में कम से कम 10 प्रतिभागी ज़रूरी थे। आवेदन 28 सितंबर 2026 को शाम 4 बजे बंद हुए, और स्वीकृत परियोजनाएँ 26 फ़रवरी 2027 तक पूरी करनी होंगी।

ul: सुनिश्चित करें कि आपके संगठन के पास वैध ABN हो और वह सही नियामक संस्था के पास पंजीकृत हो। व्यवसाय कौशल कोष के लिए दोनों ज़रूरी थे।
अपने संगठन, उसके सदस्यों और पिछले कार्यक्रमों का छोटा विवरण तैयार रखें, जिसे ज़रूरत के हिसाब से बदला जा सके।
साल की शुरुआत से ही विक्टोरियाई सरकार के बहुसांस्कृतिक अनुदान पृष्ठों पर नज़र रखें। 2026 में क्षमता निर्माण और उत्सव वाले दौर जनवरी और मार्च में घोषित हुए थे।

body.note: 2027 के कार्यक्रमों की घोषणा अभी नहीं हुई है। नियम और राशि बदल सकती हैं।

body: ਭਾਈਚਾਰਕ ਸਭਾਵਾਂ, ਮੰਦਰ, ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ, ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਗਰੁੱਪ ਅਤੇ ਵਪਾਰੀ ਸੰਘ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਫ਼ੰਡਿੰਗ ਲਈ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਬਹੁਤੇ ਗੇੜ ਸਾਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਦੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਕੁਝ ਹਫ਼ਤਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਹੇਠਾਂ ਦਿੱਤੇ 2026 ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਹੁਣ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ।

ਛੋਟੇ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਕ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਲਈ $5,000 ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਆਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਸਮਾਗਮ ਲਈ $50,000 ਤੱਕ ਦੀਆਂ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਸਨ, ਅਤੇ ਪੇਂਡੂ ਤੇ ਖੇਤਰੀ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਦੇ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਲਈ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ $1 ਮਿਲੀਅਨ ਰੱਖੇ ਗਏ। ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ, ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਾ, ਪਹੁੰਚਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਹੋਣਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸੀ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 17 ਅਪ੍ਰੈਲ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ।

$5 ਮਿਲੀਅਨ ਦੇ ਇਸ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਤਿੰਨ ਸ਼੍ਰੇਣੀਆਂ ਸਨ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੁਨਰ, ਭਾਈਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਲੀਡਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਲਈ, ਅਤੇ ਆਈਟੀ ਸਿਸਟਮ ਤੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰੀ ਯੋਜਨਾਬੰਦੀ ਵਰਗੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਖ਼ਰਚਿਆਂ ਲਈ $10,000, $100,000 ਜਾਂ $400,000 ਤੱਕ ਮਿਲ ਸਕਦੇ ਸਨ। ਨਵੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਉੱਭਰ ਰਹੇ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਿਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਪੇਂਡੂ ਤੇ ਖੇਤਰੀ ਇਲਾਕਿਆਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਸੰਸਥਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਹਿਲ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 19 ਫ਼ਰਵਰੀ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ।

ਇਸ ਫ਼ੰਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੈਰ-ਮੁਨਾਫ਼ਾ ਵਪਾਰਕ ਸੰਘਾਂ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਵਪਾਰੀ ਗਰੁੱਪਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਚੈਂਬਰ ਆਫ਼ ਕਾਮਰਸ, ਨੂੰ $5,000 ਦੀਆਂ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ, ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਉਹ ਬਹੁ-ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਛੋਟੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਾਲਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਲਾਜ਼ਮਾਂ ਲਈ ਸਲਾਹ, ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਜਾਂ ਰਹਿਨੁਮਾਈ ਦੇ ਸਕਣ। ਹਰ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਘੱਟੋ-ਘੱਟ 10 ਭਾਗੀਦਾਰ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸਨ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 28 ਸਤੰਬਰ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਮ 4 ਵਜੇ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ, ਅਤੇ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ 26 ਫ਼ਰਵਰੀ 2027 ਤੱਕ ਪੂਰੇ ਕਰਨੇ ਹੋਣਗੇ।

ul: ਯਕੀਨੀ ਬਣਾਓ ਕਿ ਤੁਹਾਡੀ ਸੰਸਥਾ ਕੋਲ ਚਾਲੂ ABN ਹੋਵੇ ਅਤੇ ਉਹ ਸਹੀ ਰੈਗੂਲੇਟਰ ਕੋਲ ਰਜਿਸਟਰਡ ਹੋਵੇ। ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰੀ ਹੁਨਰ ਫ਼ੰਡ ਲਈ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸਨ।
ਆਪਣੀ ਸੰਸਥਾ, ਇਸਦੇ ਮੈਂਬਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਛੋਟਾ ਵੇਰਵਾ ਤਿਆਰ ਰੱਖੋ, ਜਿਸਨੂੰ ਲੋੜ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਬਦਲਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ।
ਸਾਲ ਦੇ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਬਹੁ-ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਪੰਨਿਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਰੱਖੋ। 2026 ਵਿੱਚ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਤਿਉਹਾਰਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਗੇੜਾਂ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਜਨਵਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਰਚ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੀ।

body.note: 2027 ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਅਜੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਇਆ। ਨਿਯਮ ਅਤੇ ਰਕਮਾਂ ਬਦਲ ਸਕਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।

pa.dek: ਬਹੁ-ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਸੰਸਥਾਵਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨ ਫ਼ੰਡਿੰਗ ਗੇੜ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ। ਜਾਣੋ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੀ ਸੀ, ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਤੁਹਾਡੀ ਸੰਸਥਾ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾ ਸਕੇ।

body: National Australia Bank (NAB) has signed an enforceable undertaking with the Fair Work Ombudsman after underpaying about 66,000 current and former staff between 2012 and this year, AAP reported on Thursday.

The bank has agreed to pay $127 million in wages and entitlements, $34 million in interest and $8 million in superannuation, a total of about $169 million. HR Leader reported that NAB has already paid at least $155 million of it.
NAB will also make a $2 million contrition payment to the Commonwealth, the largest ever included in a Fair Work Ombudsman enforceable undertaking, according to AAP.

NAB reported the underpayments to the Ombudsman itself in late 2019, after finding significant errors in how it applied its enterprise agreement. Further problems were found in 2024 when it brought in a new agreement, HR Leader reported.

ul: Minimum wages for ordinary hours
Penalty rates, shift loadings and overtime
Annual, personal and long service leave
Superannuation

body: The Ombudsman pointed to poor record-keeping, old payroll technology and weak oversight. Fair Work Ombudsman Anna Booth said it was "particularly disappointing to see these types of large and long-running underpayment issues" at such a well-resourced employer, AAP reported.
NAB executive Sarah White said the bank took its payroll obligations "extremely seriously". "We sincerely apologise for these unintended errors," she said, according to AAP.

ul: Pay everyone affected, including for periods outside the usual legal time limits
Hire an independent auditor to check its new payroll system
Set up a steering committee led by a senior executive
Train staff on recording extra hours worked

body: One of Australia's biggest data centre companies has put the brakes on its growth after a fight with residents in Melbourne's inner west left its flagship West Footscray site short of power.

NEXTDC said on Monday it would pause all projects that do not have a customer contract, Reuters reported. Chief executive Craig Scroggie told a UBS investor conference the company "certainly didn't expect to be in the position we're in today", and linked the problem to public unease about artificial intelligence and data centres, which he described as an issue of "social license".
"That work can't restart until we clearly communicate that we've solved this problem," he said, adding that winning community support for the Melbourne site is now the top priority.

body.h: What went wrong in West Footscray

body: NEXTDC's M3 data centre sits about 10 kilometres west of the CBD and is planned to grow to 225 megawatts. To get more power, it needs electricity distributor Jemena to upgrade the local 66,000-volt network.

In September, Jemena stopped installing 15-metre power poles in neighbouring Yarraville after residents protested, with some leaving cars and bins out to block work crews, the ABC reported. Jemena cited community and stakeholder opposition, safety concerns and limited site access, and the local council has not given consent as road authority while consultation continues, according to NEXTDC. Jemena does not expect to resume before February 2027.

Residents have long raised concerns about diesel fumes and noise from the site, which they say is just 15 metres from homes. "NextDC M3 doesn't have social licence for the existing building, they certainly don't have it for an expansion," said Sean Brown, a founding member of residents' group Citizens of Tottenham. The group's president, Jacqui Glover, said the delay was "a reminder that the people living beside these developments cannot simply be pushed aside."

dl: Cut to A$475–500 million for 2026-27, from A$615–640 million
Cut to A$245–265 million, from A$385–410 million
Down about 42 per cent after the October warning, since recovered
A$4.5–5 billion this financial year, down from A$5.25–5.75 billion
Rivals Goodman Group and Digital Realty bought a 9.9 per cent stake for about A$715 million

body: Goodman and Digital Realty said they had no current plans to make a takeover offer but reserved the right to do so. NEXTDC says construction is continuing inside the existing West Footscray buildings and the affected capacity is still under contract to an unnamed customer.

NEXTDC has applied to the Victorian Government to expand the site. The company says a decision on that permit is now expected in 2027 because of caretaker rules ahead of the 28 November state election. Victoria has also announced rules to keep new data centres at least 150 metres from homes and schools, the ABC reported.
NEXTDC is due to report the outcome of a review of its building plans at its annual general meeting on 20 November.
en.dek: NEXTDC has paused every project without a signed customer after residents in Melbourne's west stopped the power upgrade its West Footscray site needs. Its chief executive says the company has to win back trust first.
en.headline: Melbourne data centre expansion halted as power delays and community opposition bite

body: One Nation has disendorsed Franco Guardiani, its candidate for the Labor-held seat of Preston in Melbourne's north, after social media posts circulated on Tuesday in which he described Adolf Hitler as the "GOAT", shorthand for "greatest of all time".

Victorian One Nation leader Warren Pickering said the party was appalled "at a time when Jewish Australians are experiencing unprecedented persecution", and that people holding such views "do not have a place in One Nation", the ABC reported. The party conceded its vetting process needed improvement.
Mr Guardiani confirmed to the ABC that the accounts were his. "The party does what it sees fit," he said, adding that he believed in free speech.

Nominations for the 28 November election closed on Monday, so Mr Guardiani will remain on the Preston ballot paper under the One Nation name, the ABC reported. One Nation volunteers are not expected to hand out how-to-vote cards at Preston polling places.
Preston is held by Labor on a margin of 2.1 per cent.
The disendorsement came on the same day Opposition Leader Jess Wilson confirmed the Coalition would put Labor, the Greens and the Socialists below One Nation on its how-to-vote cards.

body.note: A full list of candidates for every district is on the VEC website. If you see hateful content aimed at a community, Victoria's anti-vilification laws explain how to report it.

en.dek: Franco Guardiani confirmed the accounts were his. Nominations had already closed, so he will still appear under the One Nation name in the Labor-held seat.

body: Community cricket clubs can now apply for grants from a new $900,000 fund for facility upgrades that cut energy costs and make grounds more resilient to heat, storms and drought.

The Origin Community Cricket Fund is run by Cricket Australia in partnership with Origin Energy and covers the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons, according to Cricket Australia's Play Cricket website. Applications opened on Monday 9 November, The Indian Sun reported, and close on 26 February 2027.
Cricket clubs, associations, schools, councils and organisations that manage cricket facilities can apply. That includes the many community clubs in Melbourne's west, north and south-east.
Grants start at $10,000, The Indian Sun reported. Projects can include:

ul: Solar panels and battery storage
Energy-efficient lighting
Hot water systems
Electric vehicle chargers
Water tanks, irrigation and drainage
Shade for players and spectators

body: Cricket Australia says projects are guided by its national community cricket infrastructure strategy, with a focus on climate resilience and cleaner energy.
Read the fund's 2026-27 guidelines, fill in the application form and submit it through Cricket Australia's online grants portal. All three are linked from the fund's page on play.cricket.com.au.

body.note: Running a club that has applied or won a grant? Tell us about it at news@themelbourneindian.com.au.

en.dek: Clubs, associations, schools and councils can seek grants for solar panels, batteries and other facility upgrades. Applications close on 26 February 2027.

body: Parks Victoria has stopped taking new campsite bookings after a data problem at its outside booking provider, Bookeasy, and is warning customers about suspicious WhatsApp messages about their bookings.

In a statement on Wednesday, Parks Victoria said it was working urgently with Bookeasy to understand the issue and was contacting customers who might be affected. Its booking website now shows a "Booking temporarily unavailable" notice.

body.h: What it means if you have a booking

ul: Existing bookings have not been cancelled and are still valid, Parks Victoria says.
You cannot change or modify a booking for now.
New campsite bookings are suspended until further notice.

body: Bookeasy handles camping and vehicle permits for national parks in Victoria, Queensland and South Australia, ABC News reported.

In Queensland, the state's environment department said people's email addresses, home addresses and phone numbers were affected, but it did not believe payment details were accessed because payments run through a separate system. South Australia's National Parks and Wildlife Service said names, contact details and booking information may have been accessed, with no evidence that credit card details were taken. It said Bookeasy had recently detected unauthorised activity and called in cybersecurity experts.
Neither Parks Victoria nor Bookeasy has said what Victorian customers' data was involved, or how many people are affected.

ul: Parks Victoria does not contact customers on WhatsApp.
Do not click links in unexpected messages about a booking.
Do not give payment details or personal information, and do not make a payment in response to a message.
You can report scams at scamwatch.gov.au.

body.note: Check bookings.parks.vic.gov.au for updates on when bookings reopen.

en.dek: Existing bookings still stand, but no new bookings or changes can be made for now. Parks Victoria says it never contacts customers on WhatsApp.
en.headline: Parks Victoria stops campsite bookings after booking provider breach, warns of WhatsApp scams

body: RAAF Williams at Point Cook, Victoria Barracks on St Kilda Road and Fort Queenscliff will not be sold, after the federal government reversed part of its plan to sell surplus Defence land.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the change on Sunday at Victoria Barracks in Sydney, which will also stay in public hands. The ABC reported that the three Victorian sites will move from Defence to the Department of Finance rather than be sold.

Wyndham Mayor Mia Shaw said on Monday the council "welcomes the announcement that RAAF Williams will no longer be considered for sale". She said the site "should never have been considered as surplus land" and was "one of the most important aviation heritage sites in Australia". The council had made submissions to the federal government against the sale.

An audit in February identified 67 Defence sites for sale, which were expected to raise $1.8 billion, the ABC reported. Defence Minister Richard Marles said: "It is utterly untenable to be spending hundreds of millions of dollars on Defence sites" that Defence does not need.
Opposition defence spokesman James Paterson called the decision "a huge victory for the community", but said: "It's very difficult to see how the government's budget numbers now add up."

RSL Australia said more than 60 other sites were still earmarked for sale and asked the government to pause them until a Senate inquiry into Defence estate assets reports. "There's no undo button. Once a site is sold, it's gone for good," the RSL said.
en.dek: Wyndham's mayor welcomed the backdown on RAAF Williams, one of the country's most important aviation heritage sites. More than 60 other Defence sites are still earmarked for sale.

body: Qantas will cut 850 corporate jobs under a deal with the global consulting firm Accenture, and most of the work will be delivered from India, the airline told staff by email on Tuesday, AAP reported.

The first phase covers finance, procurement, human resources and marketing. Some roles will stay in Australia. ABC News reported that the changes will be phased in, with the first expected from mid-2027.

Chief executive Vanessa Hudson said the overhaul was about "modernising the technology behind our business and becoming more efficient", pointing to unwieldy back-office processes and the effect of artificial intelligence. "This is hard news for some," she said, but "standing still is not an option", according to AAP.

The Australian Services Union says Qantas is using AI as a reason to move Australian jobs offshore. Angus McFarland, the union's NSW and ACT secretary, told AAP the decision "should be chilling to not just those workers but all Australians". The union says the Sydney head office will be hit hardest. Assistant national secretary Scott Cowen called for rules to protect local jobs as AI spreads, and for transition support for affected workers.

Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles told ABC News Breakfast the decision was "disappointing" and that "it's really important that Australian jobs are a focus here". He said Qantas should work with unions so that as many staff as possible are redeployed.
AAP reported that Woolworths, Coles, Canva, NAB and ANZ have also announced or flagged moving corporate or back-office work to India, the Philippines or elsewhere in Asia.
Qantas reported a 2025-26 net profit of about $1.3 billion in August, down almost 20 per cent, after high jet fuel costs, and has warned fares could rise again in 2027.

body.note: If your job is affected, your union or the Fair Work Ombudsman (13 13 94) can explain redundancy and consultation rights. This is general information, not legal advice.

en.dek: Finance, procurement, HR and marketing staff are first in line. Qantas blames clunky systems and AI; unions call it offshoring, and the Acting Prime Minister says it is disappointing.

body: Victoria's election is still more than two weeks away, but one count is already in. Ramayana: Part One was the most-watched film in Australia on its opening weekend, taking about $2.72 million from Thursday 5 November to Sunday 8 November, Variety Australia reported.

Trade publication B&T reported the film sold about 117,000 tickets over the weekend. Japan's Godzilla Minus Zero came second with $1.31 million for the weekend, according to Variety Australia ($1.6 million and about 55,000 tickets once IMAX preview screenings are included, B&T reported).
B&T reported it was the first time two foreign-language films finished first and second across a weekend at the Australian box office. The pair also held the top two spots on opening day.

"Two films in two different languages outsold every English-language release in the country," said Guy Burbidge, managing director of cinema advertising company Val Morgan Cinema. "This weekend shows how much Australia's culturally and linguistically diverse audiences are shaping cinema."

body: At 11am today, Melbourne will pause for a minute. The Victorian State Remembrance Service begins at 10.30am at the Shrine of Remembrance, and anyone can attend without booking. For most Australians, the minute's silence brings to mind the diggers of Gallipoli and the Western Front. Fewer know that the men beside them in the trenches included thousands of soldiers from what was then undivided India.

Speaking at the Anzac Day dawn service in New Delhi this year, Australia's High Commissioner to India, Philip Green, put the number at around 16,000 troops from India who served at Gallipoli, with around 1,600 of them dying there. Sikh, Punjabi Muslim and Gurkha soldiers fought in battles such as Chunuk Bair and Hill 60, and Indian muleteers, stretcher-bearers and medical orderlies carried supplies under fire and tended the wounded.

Mr Green cited the historian Peter Stanley, who has argued that the Indian contribution at Gallipoli was as great as that of the ANZACs themselves. Photographs held by the Australian War Memorial show Indian soldiers on the landing beach at Anzac Cove, Indian gunners beside an Australian rest camp, and Indian mule teams camped at the head of what the diggers called Mule Gully.

The Australians noticed. In a letter home in 1915, Private Charlie Beherendt wrote that he had been "fighting side by side with Kitchener's army, and the Sikhs and Gurkhas", adding: "The Indians fight like tigers and are a great unit to the Empire."

body.h: The Indian Australians who enlisted anyway

body: Australia's Defence Act of 1909 said that people "not substantially of European origin or descent" were not eligible to enlist. Even so, the Australian War Memorial has identified at least 12 Indian Australians who joined the Australian Imperial Force in the First World War.

Two of them never came home. Nain Singh Sailani was born in Shimla and came to Western Australia in 1895, working as a labourer in Perth. He enlisted in February 1916, at the age of 43, and joined the 44th Battalion on the Western Front. He was killed on 1 June 1917 during a trench raid in Belgium and is buried at Strand Military Cemetery.

Sarn Singh came from Jullundur in Punjab and farmed near Loxton in South Australia's Riverland. He enlisted in May 1916, at about 38, and joined the 43rd Battalion. He was killed on 10 June 1917 during the advance on Messines Ridge, when enemy artillery struck his position.

A third, Desanda Singh of Kapurthala, a travelling salesman who settled near Ceduna, served with the 3rd Light Horse in Egypt in 1918 and came home. He was still working as a hawker in South Australia in 1946.

In July this year, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission added 9,909 Indian Army servicemen of the First World War to its official casualty records, the largest single addition since the Second World War. Most had died in India, away from the fighting fronts, and rulings by the British Indian government at the time denied them war-graves status, so their names were never passed on.

The names were recovered from the Punjab Registers, held at the Lahore Museum, which record the service of about 320,000 Punjabi recruits. The five-year project was run by the CWGC with the UK Punjab Heritage Association and the University of Greenwich. The men are now listed in an online book of remembrance, and families can search for them by name on the CWGC website.
"The recovery of every one of these 9,909 names helps restore missing chapters in family and world histories," the commission's director general, Claire Horton, said at the time.

The Victorian State Remembrance Service starts at 10.30am at the Second World War Memorial Forecourt of the Shrine of Remembrance, on St Kilda Road. No booking is needed, though seating is limited, and the service is also streamed online. At 11am the Shrine's Ray of Light falls on the word "Love" on the Stone of Remembrance, marking the moment the Armistice was signed in 1918; the public can see the alignment again at midday. Veterans, war widows and widowers travel free on public transport today.

body.note: The Gallipoli figures are the Australian High Commissioner's and are described as approximate. The Australian War Memorial says at least 12 Indian Australians enlisted; the true number may be higher, because some enlisted under anglicised names.

en.dek: Around 16,000 soldiers from India served at Gallipoli in 1915, and at least 12 Indian Australians joined the AIF despite a law that said they couldn't. This year, nearly 10,000 more Indian soldiers of the First World War were finally added to the official records.
en.headline: At Gallipoli, the ANZACs weren't alone: the Indian soldiers Remembrance Day forgets

body: A Hindu temple in Melbourne's west was left without power on the eve of Diwali after its electricity was cut for the second time in eight days, according to MPs from both major parties. The incidents were first reported by The Indian Sun and South Asia Times.

Evan Mulholland, the Opposition's spokesman for multicultural and multifaith affairs, said power to the SMVS Swaminarayan temple in Mount Cottrell, next to Tarneit, was cut on Saturday 31 October, and the community paid thousands of dollars to have it reconnected. He said vandals returned on Saturday 7 November, the night before Diwali, and cut the power again at the main electrical board. The temple could not restore it in time for its celebrations, he said.
"No faith community in Victoria should have to live like this," Mr Mulholland said in a statement on Sunday, The Indian Sun reported.

body.note: The details of the power cuts come from MPs' statements. The Melbourne Indian has not been able to confirm them with Victoria Police, which had not commented publicly at the time of publication. No one has been charged and the motive is not known.

body: Tarneit's Labor MP, Dylan Wight, visited the temple on Sunday. He told The Indian Sun he was "deeply disappointed and concerned by the latest act of vandalism", and that no community should have to keep repairing damage to its place of worship.

Mr Wight also told the paper that Labor would provide $200,000 for security upgrades at the temple if it is re-elected on 28 November, with the work to be decided with temple management. How the money would be paid and when work could start have not been announced.

The Liberal candidate for Tarneit, Venkat Ram Upparlapalle, visited the temple last week and called for a thorough police investigation, stronger security and accountability. "A temple should be a place of peace, prayer and belonging," he wrote on social media.

Earlier this month Premier Ben Carroll announced an $11 million Temple and Gurdwara Safety Fund, for security and other upgrades at Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras, at the Sri Durga Temple in Deanside. South Asia Times reported that the Deanside temple would receive $1 million. The Melbourne Indian could not find a Coalition funding commitment for the SMVS temple at the time of publication.

Mr Mulholland said the temple had faced theft, break-ins, a firebombing, a vehicle being driven into the building and repeated interference with its power over more than a decade, sometimes before major festivals, The Indian Sun reported.

After a break-in before Holi in March 2025, temple trustee Biren Joshi told The Australia Today it was the eighth incident in eight years, and that no arrests had been made for any of them. The temple has received government money for security before: The Indian Sun reported that funding for fencing, gates and CCTV was set aside for it under the federal Safer Communities Fund in 2020.
Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or at crimestoppersvic.com.au, and can stay anonymous. In an emergency, call triple zero (000).
en.dek: The SMVS Swaminarayan temple near Tarneit lost power twice in eight days, according to MPs from both major parties. Labor has pledged $200,000 for its security if re-elected.
